concepts.name: Coherent and dissipative dynamics on an equal footing
concepts.statement: Atomic physics is approached through a unified picture of coherent evolution and environmental decoherence and dissipation, and to understand the dynamics of the systems studied both must be treated on an equal footing.

concepts.name: Simple systems
concepts.statement: A theoretical understanding is built first for simple systems, those where only a few states, a few particles, or a few quanta are relevant; more complex systems are then understood by combining these building blocks.

concepts.name: State vector
concepts.statement: The most complete knowledge of the system is contained in the state vector, an element of a Hilbert space, which can be expanded in any orthonormal basis.

concepts.name: Expansion coefficient
concepts.statement: The projection of the state on a basis state gives the expansion coefficient of the state in that basis.

concepts.name: Probability of a basis state
concepts.statement: The probability of finding the system in a basis state is the squared modulus of its expansion coefficient.

concepts.name: Superposition and interference
concepts.statement: For a superposition of states the probability of a basis state is the absolute value squared of the sum of amplitudes, not the sum of probabilities; the difference is the interference term.

concepts.name: Observable
concepts.statement: Observables are represented by Hermitian operators acting on states of the Hilbert space.

concepts.name: Expectation value
concepts.statement: The expectation value of an observable in a state is the average of its eigenvalues weighted by the probabilities of the eigenstates.

concepts.name: Commutator
concepts.statement: Operators in general do not commute; when their commutator is nonzero they do not have the same eigenstates.

concepts.name: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle
concepts.statement: For any two operators the product of their uncertainties is at least half the expectation value of their commutator.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian is the operator of the system's energy that generates its time evolution; its eigenstates are the stationary states.

concepts.name: Schrodinger's equation
concepts.statement: In Schrodinger's picture the state vector evolves in time according to Schrodinger's equation while the operators are stationary.

concepts.name: Stationary states
concepts.statement: The stationary solutions of Schrodinger's equation are the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian.

concepts.name: Time evolution in the energy eigenbasis
concepts.statement: Expanded in the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian, each coefficient of a state only acquires the phase of its energy.

concepts.name: Time evolution operator
concepts.statement: Formally integrating the time evolution equation gives the operator that carries the initial state to the state at time t.

concepts.name: Heisenberg's equation of motion
concepts.statement: In Heisenberg's picture the state does not evolve; the observables depend on time and evolve according to Heisenberg's equation of motion.

concepts.name: Hydrogen atom Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: Hydrogen is one electron bound by the Coulomb force to a proton, with energy the electron's kinetic energy plus the Coulomb potential.

concepts.name: Hydrogen bound-state energies
concepts.statement: Hydrogen has an infinite set of discrete bound states with energies -R∞/n² and a continuum of unbound states with positive energy.

concepts.name: Rydberg's constant
concepts.statement: The binding energy of the hydrogen ground state for an infinitely heavy nucleus.

concepts.name: Estimating a binding energy from the uncertainty principle
concepts.statement: Taking Heisenberg's inequality as an equality in the ground state and minimizing the resulting average energy over the size of the state estimates its binding energy.

concepts.name: Degeneracy and symmetry
concepts.statement: An operator that commutes with the Hamiltonian shares its eigenvectors, and the energy does not depend on its eigenvalue: level degeneracies come from symmetries, invariance under a set of unitary transformations.

concepts.name: Principal quantum number
concepts.statement: The quantum number n on which alone the energies of the hydrogen atom depend; all angular momentum states l = 0, …, n−1 share it.

concepts.name: Lifting of the L degeneracy
concepts.statement: Deviations of the potential from 1/r, such as the screening of the nuclear charge by inner electrons, make the energy a function of both n and l, with large l states less deeply bound.

concepts.name: Rydberg states
concepts.statement: Very large n states, whose reduced splitting between different l makes their spectra nearly hydrogen-like.

concepts.name: Fine structure
concepts.statement: Relativistic corrections, the kinetic-energy correction, the spin-orbit term and the Darwin term, split each principal level so that different J have different energies.

concepts.name: Total electronic angular momentum
concepts.statement: The sum of the orbital and spin angular momenta of the electron, whose quantum numbers label the states once spin-orbit coupling acts.

concepts.name: Spin-orbit interaction
concepts.statement: The interaction of the electron's spin magnetic dipole with the atom's internal magnetic field, which splits the J = 3/2 and J = 1/2 levels of a P state by A.

concepts.name: Darwin term
concepts.statement: A relativistic correction to the potential energy that acts only at the origin and so is nonzero only for L = 0 states.

concepts.name: D1 and D2 lines
concepts.statement: The transitions from the sodium ground state to the P₁/₂ and P₃/₂ excited states.

concepts.name: Parity of hydrogen-like wavefunctions
concepts.statement: A hydrogen-like wavefunction is a radial function times a spherical harmonic, and its parity is (−1)^l.

concepts.name: Hyperfine interaction
concepts.statement: The interaction of the valence electron's magnetic dipole with the nuclear spin, strongest for S states through the contact term.

concepts.name: Total angular momentum F
concepts.statement: With fine and hyperfine interactions the conserved quantum number is the total angular momentum, nuclear spin plus electronic.

concepts.name: Hyperfine structure of the alkali ground state
concepts.statement: The hydrogen ground state splits into F = 0 and 1 by A_HFS/2; the ground states of ²³Na and ⁸⁷Rb into F = 1 and 2 by 3A_HFS/2.

concepts.name: Zeeman effect
concepts.statement: In a static external magnetic field the energy levels shift by the interaction of the magnetic moments with the field.

concepts.name: Bohr magneton
concepts.statement: The unit of atomic magnetic moment in which the electron and nuclear moments are written through their g-factors.

concepts.name: Strong and weak field regimes
concepts.statement: In a strong field m_S and m_I are good quantum numbers; in a weak field F and m_F are.

concepts.name: Clebsch-Gordan coefficients
concepts.statement: The coefficients relating the coupled basis |J, m_J⟩ to the product basis of two angular momenta.

concepts.name: Weak-field Zeeman shift
concepts.statement: At low field the Zeeman effect is a perturbation on the fine and hyperfine levels, and the shift of |F, m_F⟩ is proportional to the field.

concepts.name: Lande g-factor
concepts.statement: The factors g_J and g_F that scale the Zeeman shift of a J or F level.

concepts.name: Electric dipole interaction
concepts.statement: A neutral atom in an electric field develops an electric dipole moment that interacts with the field; off resonance the levels shift, near resonance transitions occur.

concepts.name: Dipole matrix element
concepts.statement: Transitions between two states are possible only when the matrix element of the dipole operator between them is nonzero.

concepts.name: Selection rules
concepts.statement: The restrictions on the states between which the dipole matrix element is nonzero: ΔL = ±1, ΔS = 0, ΔJ and ΔF = ±1, 0 with 0 → 0 forbidden.

concepts.name: Magnetic selection rules
concepts.statement: The change of the magnetic quantum number is set by the light's polarization: +1 for σ⁺, −1 for σ⁻ and 0 for ẑ light.

concepts.name: Circular polarization components
concepts.statement: An electric field written as right and left circularly polarized and ẑ linearly polarized components.

concepts.name: Two-level atom
concepts.statement: An atom may be approximated as a two-level system when the external field is weak and nearly on resonance with a single atomic transition, so that only the ground state and the near-resonant excited level have appreciable probability of occupation.

concepts.name: Atomic transition frequency
concepts.statement: The energy difference of the two atomic levels is ħω.

concepts.name: Nearly-monochromatic classical field
concepts.statement: A nearly-monochromatic classical field oscillates at the optical frequency ν with a slowly-varying envelope that varies on a timescale much slower than the optical frequency and a length scale much larger than the optical wavelength.

concepts.name: Optical frequency of the field
concepts.statement: The angular frequency ν of the applied field, near the atomic transition frequency.

concepts.name: Dipole operator of a two-level atom
concepts.statement: Truncated to the two relevant levels, which carry no permanent dipole, the dipole operator only connects the two states through the dipole matrix elements.

concepts.name: Two-level atom in a classical field
concepts.statement: The full Hamiltonian of the two-level atom and classical field is the excited-level energy minus the coupling of the atomic dipole to the field.

concepts.name: Two-level equations of motion
concepts.statement: Expanding the state in the eigenstates of the free Hamiltonian, Schroedinger's equation gives coupled differential equations for the probability amplitudes c₁(t) and c₂(t).

concepts.name: Detuning
concepts.statement: The difference between the optical frequency of the field and the atomic transition frequency.

concepts.name: Rotating frame
concepts.statement: Defining a slowly varying amplitude removes the fast phase evolution at the optical frequency and the explicitly time dependent terms from the equations of motion.

concepts.name: Rabi frequency
concepts.statement: The frequency at which the dynamics of the driven atom occur, the field envelope times the dipole matrix element over ħ.

concepts.name: Rotating wave approximation
concepts.statement: When the field is near resonance and weak, the terms oscillating at twice the optical frequency have little effect on average and are neglected, leaving equations for the slowly varying amplitudes with no explicit time dependence.

concepts.name: Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: On resonance the amplitudes evolve as sines and cosines and the populations of the two levels oscillate out of phase at the Rabi frequency, the periodic absorption and stimulated emission of radiation.

concepts.name: Polarization of the atom
concepts.statement: The instantaneous polarization of the atom is the expectation of the dipole moment operator, which varies both on the fast optical timescale and on the slower timescale of the populations.

concepts.name: Pulse area
concepts.statement: When the applied field amplitude varies in time without a chirp, the amplitudes depend only on the total area under the applied field.

concepts.name: Adiabatic elimination
concepts.statement: For a far-detuned field the fast-oscillating part of the excited amplitude averages to zero, so one sets its derivative to zero and the excited amplitude adiabatically follows the ground amplitude.

concepts.name: AC Stark shift
concepts.statement: A far off resonant field shifts the lower state energy by |Ω|²/δ.

concepts.name: Effective Hamiltonian in the rotating frame
concepts.statement: The original Hamiltonian after the RWA, written in the rotating frame, has no explicit time dependence.

concepts.name: Bare states
concepts.statement: The eigenstates of the system when no applied field is present.

concepts.name: Dressed states
concepts.statement: The eigenvectors of the rotating-frame Hamiltonian are mixtures of the bare atomic states; on resonance they are their symmetric and antisymmetric combinations, and far off resonance they resemble the bare states with a small admixture of the other.

concepts.name: Dressed state energies
concepts.statement: The eigenenergies of the dressed states, split by twice the Rabi frequency on resonance and close to the bare energies far off resonance.

concepts.name: Bloch sphere
concepts.statement: The state of the two-level system can be represented as a vector on the unit sphere, |2⟩ pointing along +ẑ and |1⟩ along −ẑ, with the spin operators of a two-level system as its components.

concepts.name: Precession on the Bloch sphere
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian acts as an effective magnetic field, and the Bloch vector precesses about the drive vector made of the field and the detuning.

concepts.name: Rotating frame for multistate systems
concepts.statement: A time-dependent unitary transformation that rotates each atomic state at its associated optical frequency gives a time independent Hamiltonian, so long as no atomic transition is linked by more than one applied field.

concepts.name: Floquet basis
concepts.statement: When two fields are near resonance with one transition, the amplitudes are expanded in a Fourier series in the beatnote frequency, whose components are all coupled.

concepts.name: Bound to continuum transition
concepts.statement: A transition from a bound state to the continuum of unbound states, treated by discretizing the continuum in a box whose size approaches infinity.

concepts.name: Continuum without memory
concepts.statement: Summed over a densely spaced continuum, the exponentials cancel except at t = t′, so the continuum acts on the bound state locally in time and has no memory of earlier configurations.

concepts.name: Principal value identity
concepts.statement: An identity from complex analysis splits the limit into a delta function and a principal value.

concepts.name: Decay into a continuum
concepts.statement: Coupling to the continuum makes the bound state population decay exponentially at the rate γ, precisely the rate Fermi's Golden Rule gives.

concepts.name: Fermi's Golden Rule
concepts.statement: First order perturbation theory gives a transition rate into a continuum, which the long time treatment reproduces because the continuum has no memory.

concepts.name: AC Stark shift from the continuum
concepts.statement: The continuum states also shift the bound state energy, most important for sub-threshold illumination, where the decay vanishes.

concepts.name: Outgoing wavepacket
concepts.statement: At long times the system is in a superposition of continuum states forming an outgoing wavepacket propagating away from the atom, behaviour that seems irreversible yet comes from unitary evolution.

concepts.name: Spontaneous emission
concepts.statement: Real atoms decay from an excited state even with no applied field, through their interaction with the vacuum modes of the field, which requires a quantum mechanical treatment of the electromagnetic field.

concepts.name: Modes of a periodic cavity
concepts.statement: A field in a large cavity with periodic boundary conditions has running-wave eigenmodes with allowed wavevectors, two polarizations to each.

concepts.name: Mode expansion of the field
concepts.statement: An arbitrary excitation is expanded in the spatial modes, each with a time-dependent coordinate normalized to be the position of a harmonic oscillator.

concepts.name: Mode position and momentum
concepts.statement: Quantization identifies each mode's coordinate and its time derivative with non-commuting position and momentum operators, as for a harmonic oscillator of unit mass.

concepts.name: Creation and annihilation operators
concepts.statement: Operators that create and annihilate excitations of each mode and polarization.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian of the quantized field
concepts.statement: The classical energy within the cavity is that of a set of harmonic oscillators, one per mode, with energy ħν_j per excitation and a vacuum energy of half that.

concepts.name: Quantized electric field
concepts.statement: The electric field operator expanded in running-wave excitations, divided into its positive and negative frequency components.

concepts.name: Electric field of a single photon
concepts.statement: The electric field associated with a single photon, a figure of merit for any phenomena relying on atomic interactions with a vacuum field.

concepts.name: Atom interacting with the quantized field
concepts.statement: Replacing the field in the dipole Hamiltonian by its operator gives four terms, of which only emission with decay and absorption with excitation conserve energy; the other two are the fast-rotating terms the RWA drops.

concepts.name: Single-photon Rabi frequency
concepts.statement: The coupling constant of the atom to one mode, the frequency at which an atom spontaneously emits and reabsorbs a single resonant photon.

concepts.name: Transverse fields and gauge
concepts.statement: Quantizing a source-free field treats only transverse fields, which avoids the vector potential and corresponds to an implicit choice of gauge; the canonical Hamiltonian with the momentum p − qA/c is the more general approach.

concepts.name: Wigner-Weisskopf theory
concepts.statement: Projected onto the excited atom with no photon and the ground atom with one photon, spontaneous emission is a bound to continuum transition.

concepts.name: Lamb shift
concepts.statement: The shift of the energy levels from the atom-field interaction, usually incorporated into a renormalized transition frequency, which changes in a different environment such as a cavity.

concepts.name: Spontaneous emission rate
concepts.statement: The excited atom decays at a rate proportional to the square of the atomic dipole moment and the cube of the transition frequency.

concepts.name: Decay of the atomic dipole
concepts.statement: For an atom starting in a superposition, the atomic dipole moment decays as e^{−γt/2}, unlike classical Rabi oscillations, with no buildup of atomic coherences.

concepts.name: Wavepacket of the emitted photon
concepts.statement: The field emitted spontaneously has zero mean electric field and no first order coherence, but its one-photon amplitude describes a wavepacket outgoing from the atom at speed c with an exponentially decaying tail.

concepts.name: Polarization of light
concepts.statement: Each wavevector $\mathbf{k}$ carries two modes, one for each polarization vector $\epsilon_\alpha$ orthogonal to $\mathbf{k}$; the mode index $j$ includes both the mode number and the polarization of the wave.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo wavefunction
concepts.statement: The master equation can be simulated by a stochastic wavefunction: a state vector that evolves under an effective Hamiltonian and jumps at random, whose average over many trajectories gives the density matrix.

concepts.name: General form of the master equation
concepts.statement: The most general form of the master equation allowed by physics adds to the coherent evolution a Liouvillian built from arbitrary operators ĉ_k with rates γ_k; the thermal reservoir's master equation is the case ĉ_{2k} = √(n̄+1)Ŝ_k, ĉ_{2k+1} = √n̄ Ŝ_k†.

concepts.name: Effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: The first two terms of the master equation act like evolution under an effective Hamiltonian, the system Hamiltonian with an imaginary part −iℏΣγ_k ĉ_k†ĉ_k/2; it is not Hermitian, so it does not conserve the norm.

concepts.name: Quantum jump
concepts.statement: The last term of the master equation is a quantum jump operator that changes |ψ_α⟩ into the state ĉ_k|ψ_α⟩ with some probability.

concepts.name: Jump probability
concepts.statement: In a small time δt the state jumps through channel k with probability δp_{k,α} = δtγ_k⟨ψ_α|ĉ_k†ĉ_k|ψ_α⟩, and through any channel with δp_α, the norm lost by the no-jump evolution.

concepts.name: No-jump evolution
concepts.statement: A system that has not jumped evolves in discrete time under the effective Hamiltonian and is renormalized by √(1 − δp_α).

concepts.name: Master equation as jump statistics
concepts.statement: Written in discrete time with normalized states, the master equation says that after δt the system evolves under Ĥ_eff with probability 1 − δp_α, or jumps into |φ̃_{k,α}⟩ with probability δp_{k,α}.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo procedure
concepts.statement: Simulate the master equation by evolving a state vector step by step, drawing a random number each step to decide between no-jump evolution and a jump, repeating for N trajectories and averaging them into the density matrix.

concepts.name: Monte Carlo decay of a two-level atom
concepts.statement: A decaying two-level atom jumps with probability δtγ|a₂|² per step; if it does not jump, its excited population decays more slowly than e^{−γt}, while the average over trajectories decays as e^{−γt}.

concepts.name: Not detecting a photon is a measurement
concepts.statement: Not detecting a photon is also a measurement on the system: it makes the state evolve so that at long times the atom ends up in |1⟩ even if it never emits a photon.

concepts.name: When to use the Monte Carlo method
concepts.statement: The Monte Carlo method is advantageous when the Hilbert space is too large for the density matrix or when measurement-dependent feedback is wanted; otherwise it is a method of last resort.

concepts.name: Non-Hermitian evolution
concepts.statement: Where quantum jumps are improbable over the time considered, a system can be treated by the non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation alone, the imaginary parts of the energy accounting for finite lifetimes; probability then leaks from the system without the record of where it goes.

concepts.name: Macroscopic polarization
concepts.statement: The polarization of an atomic ensemble is the dipole moment per volume of the atoms in a small volume, each atom contributing ⟨d̂⟩ = μρ₂₁ + μ*ρ₁₂; it varies in space as the fields do.

concepts.name: Independent atoms
concepts.statement: An ensemble may be treated atom by atom with the single-atom optical Bloch equations when the atoms do not interact strongly, each is damped by its own reservoir (|r_i − r_j| > λ), and the applied field is classical; the ensemble density matrix then factorizes into a product of single-atom density matrices.

concepts.name: Maxwell equations with a polarization source
concepts.statement: Self-consistency requires the polarization the field induces to act back as a source term in the Maxwell equations governing the light.

concepts.name: Wave equation with a polarization source
concepts.statement: Without unbound charges and currents the Maxwell equations become a wave equation for E driven by the second time derivative of the polarization.

concepts.name: Slowly-varying envelope approximation
concepts.statement: A nearly monochromatic field and its polarization are written as envelopes on a carrier of central frequency ν̄ and wavevector k̄ = ν̄/c; keeping only the lowest derivatives of envelopes that vary slowly on the optical period and wavelength reduces the second-order wave equation to first order.

concepts.name: Slowly varying polarization
concepts.statement: The slowly varying polarization amplitude 𝒫 is the envelope of the polarization on the carrier; it is proportional to the positive-frequency component of the dipole operator in the rotating frame, 𝒫 = (N/V)μρ₂₁(z)e^{−ik̄z} for two-level atoms.

concepts.name: Propagation equation for slowly varying amplitudes
concepts.statement: In the slowly-varying envelope approximation the envelope obeys a first-order equation: transverse diffraction, propagation at c, and the slowly varying polarization as the source.

concepts.name: Plane-wave propagation equation
concepts.statement: For a plane wave the transverse term vanishes and the envelope obeys ∂𝓔/∂z + (1/c)∂𝓔/∂t = (ik̄/2ε₀)𝒫.

concepts.name: Optical frequency comb
concepts.statement: A periodic train of short optical pulses is a comb of harmonics in the Fourier domain: the harmonic spacing sets the repetition rate and the occupied bandwidth the pulse duration.

concepts.name: SVEA for many harmonics
concepts.statement: When each harmonic has a slowly varying envelope, the propagation equation holds harmonic by harmonic, for arbitrarily short pulses; the atomic response couples the harmonics, giving the coupled Maxwell-Bloch equations.

concepts.name: Susceptibility
concepts.statement: When the atoms respond linearly the polarization is proportional to the field, and the constant of proportionality, the susceptibility χ, entirely characterizes the atom-photon interaction in the linear regime.

concepts.name: General solution for linear propagation
concepts.statement: In the linear regime each frequency component of the field propagates separately, acquiring the phase z(δν/c + k̄χ(δν)/2); transforming back to time gives the field anywhere from its spectrum at one place.

concepts.name: Absorption coefficient
concepts.statement: The imaginary part of the susceptibility attenuates or amplifies the beam intensity exponentially with distance at the rate α = k̄ Im[χ(0)].

concepts.name: Index of refraction
concepts.statement: The real part of the susceptibility shifts the phase of the field linearly with distance, a change of wavevector k̄ → k̄ + k̄Re[χ]/2, or of the index of refraction.

concepts.name: Dispersion
concepts.statement: Dispersion results from the frequency dependence of the susceptibility; expanding χ about resonance, the first term gives refraction, the second the group velocity, the third group velocity dispersion.

concepts.name: Group velocity
concepts.statement: Keeping the slope of the susceptibility, the envelope propagates unchanged in shape at the group velocity v_g.

concepts.name: Susceptibility of two-level atoms
concepts.statement: For a dilute gas of two-level atoms in the steady state the susceptibility is a Lorentzian of linewidth γ₁₂, proportional to the density, λ³ and the population difference.

concepts.name: Absorption on resonance
concepts.statement: On resonance the susceptibility is purely imaginary: there is no refraction but there is absorption, and the field decays exponentially.

concepts.name: Absorption cross-section
concepts.statement: The intensity decays as I(z) = I(0)e^{−Nσ̃z/V}, defining the absorption cross-section σ̃ = (3/4π)λ²γ/γ₁₂.

concepts.name: Unitary limit
concepts.statement: For purely radiative broadening the resonant cross section is 3λ²/2π, independent of the dipole moment: the maximal absorption cross section, the unitary limit.

concepts.name: Far-detuned medium is refractive
concepts.statement: Far from resonance Im[χ] ∝ 1/δν² is much smaller than Re[χ] ∝ 1/δν, so the medium is almost entirely refractive and absorbs little.

concepts.name: Homogeneous broadening
concepts.statement: A homogeneous linewidth comes from processes that affect every atom equally.

concepts.name: Inhomogeneous broadening
concepts.statement: Inhomogeneous broadening widens the line of an ensemble but not of its constituent atoms, which see different transition frequencies (local fields in solids, Doppler shifts in a thermal gas); it can hide the homogeneous linewidth.

concepts.name: Doppler broadening
concepts.statement: An atom of velocity v_z sees the field shifted to ν − kv_z, so a thermal gas absorbs each frequency through one velocity class; summing the velocity classes gives a Lorentzian spectrum for γ₁₂ ≫ kv_T and a Gaussian of width ~kv_T in the opposite limit, which grows as the square root of the temperature.

concepts.name: Cross section of a Doppler-broadened gas
concepts.statement: Inhomogeneous broadening reduces the resonant cross section by about γ₁₂/kv_T.

concepts.name: Nonlinear susceptibility
concepts.statement: For a strong continuous-wave field in the steady state, the saturated population difference γ/(γ + 2R_opt) multiplies the linear susceptibility; χ_n applies only to continuous-wave steady states.

concepts.name: Nonlinear propagation of a continuous-wave field
concepts.statement: For a continuous-wave field the time derivatives drop and ∂𝓔/∂z is set by χ_n, which depends on the field through R_opt: as the field grows, the absorption diminishes.

concepts.name: Saturation parameter
concepts.statement: The saturation parameter s = 2R_opt/γ, on resonance 4|Ω|²/γ₁₂γ, compares the optical pumping rate with decay; for s ≫ 1 the field bleaches the medium.

concepts.name: Saturation on resonance
concepts.statement: On resonance Im[χ_n] falls as 1/(1+s); a field near the saturation intensity first decays linearly with distance and then, once weak, exponentially.

concepts.name: Kerr effect
concepts.statement: Far from resonance the refractive index depends on the intensity, n = n₀ + n₂I, which gives self-phase modulation and self-focussing or de-focussing of a finite beam.

concepts.name: Third-order susceptibility
concepts.statement: For weak fields the susceptibility expands as χ + χ⁽³⁾|E|² + …, χ⁽³⁾ being the leading nonlinear correction in a system with inversion symmetry.

concepts.name: Saturation intensity
concepts.statement: A radiatively broadened transition saturates at resonance when 8|Ω|² ≈ γ², an intensity of a few mW/cm² for the alkali atoms; in a Doppler-broadened gas that field saturates only one velocity class.

concepts.name: Optical pumping
concepts.statement: With another long-lived level the excited atom can decay out of the driven transition, so population ends up there and saturation needs R_opt only to exceed that slow decay.

concepts.name: Saturation spectroscopy
concepts.statement: Two counterpropagating beams of one frequency, a strong pump and a weak probe, address the velocity classes ν = Δ ± kv_z; near resonance both address the stationary atoms, and the probe absorption shows a sharp feature with the natural linewidth inside the Doppler profile.

concepts.name: Saturated absorption dip
concepts.statement: To lowest order in the pump the probe absorption has a dip of Doppler-free width γ₁₂ at δ = 0.

concepts.name: Instantaneous eigenstates
concepts.statement: At any given time t₀ the Hamiltonian Ĥ(t₀) has instantaneous eigenstates |ϵ_k(t₀)⟩ and eigenvalues ϵ_k(t₀), and an arbitrary state may be expanded in them.

concepts.name: Coupling by changing eigenstates
concepts.statement: The time dependence of the instantaneous eigenstates couples their amplitudes through the off-diagonal terms −iℏ⟨ϵ_k|ϵ̇_l⟩, so an eigenstate of a time-dependent Hamiltonian is not in general stationary.

concepts.name: Adiabatic theorem
concepts.statement: A system prepared in an instantaneous eigenstate of a Hamiltonian that changes slowly enough stays in that eigenstate as it evolves: this is the adiabatic limit, where negligible population leaks to other states.

concepts.name: Adiabaticity condition
concepts.statement: The instantaneous eigenstate is stationary when the coupling ℏ|⟨ϵ_l|ϵ̇_k⟩| to every other eigenstate is small compared to their energy difference; a Hamiltonian changing on a timescale τ gives couplings ∝ 1/τ.

concepts.name: Dynamical phase
concepts.statement: The dynamical phase e^{−i/ℏ∫ϵ_k dτ} comes from the diagonal part of the Schrödinger equation.

concepts.name: Geometric phase
concepts.statement: Even when the adiabaticity condition is satisfied, the neglected diagonal terms ⟨ϵ_k|ϵ̇_k⟩ may introduce a geometric or Berry's phase, added to the dynamical phase.

concepts.name: Mixing angle
concepts.statement: The mixing angle θ sets how much of each bare state the dressed states of a two-level system contain; it is fixed by the ratio of the Rabi frequency to the detuning.

concepts.name: Time-dependent dressed states
concepts.statement: For a two-level system with time-dependent detuning and Rabi frequency, the instantaneous eigenstates |±⟩ and eigenenergies ϵ± are a set of time-dependent dressed states and dressed energies.

concepts.name: Adiabatic return
concepts.statement: With the detuning held constant and nonzero, a pulse Ω(t) takes a system adiabatically following |−⟩ into a superposition of |1⟩ and |2⟩ and, as the pulse ends, back to its initial state |1⟩.

concepts.name: Rapid adiabatic passage
concepts.statement: Chirping the detuning through resonance while sending in a pulse carries the system along the avoided crossing from |1⟩ to |2⟩ with near unit probability, robustly against imprecise Δ, Ω and τ; it can be faster than the excited-state lifetime, hence “rapid”.

concepts.name: Adiabaticity condition for the two-level system
concepts.statement: The two-level system follows |−⟩ when ℏθ̇ is small compared to the splitting ϵ₊ − ϵ₋ ≥ 2ℏΩ, which for passage amounts to a pulse area A ≫ 1 and a minimum time τ ≈ 1/Ω.

concepts.name: Landau-Zener model
concepts.statement: For constant Ω₀ and a detuning swept linearly, Δ = αt, the probability of complete transfer is P_LZ = 1 − e^{−2π|Ω₀|²/|α|}; its non-adiabatic correction is not analytic in the small parameter and cannot be found by perturbation theory.

concepts.name: Dressed states of the three-level system
concepts.statement: At two-photon resonance the three-level Hamiltonian has dressed states |Φ±⟩ and |Φ₀⟩; |Φ₀⟩, with energy zero and no overlap with |3⟩, is the dark state, a superposition of |1⟩ and |2⟩ set by tan θ = Ω₁/Ω₂.

concepts.name: Stimulated Raman adiabatic passage
concepts.statement: Sweeping the mixing angle slowly from 0 to π/2 with a counterintuitive pulse sequence carries the dark state from |1⟩ to −|2⟩ without ever populating |3⟩; the transfer is robust to pulse shape and timing and to the single-photon detuning, but sensitive to the two-photon detuning.

concepts.name: Four-level dark states
concepts.statement: Three metastable states resonantly coupled to one excited state have two degenerate dark states; because they are degenerate their nonadiabatic coupling can be used to prepare an arbitrary superposition c₃|3⟩ + c₄|4⟩, set by the phase and amplitude of the third field.

concepts.name: Adiabatic beamsplitter for atoms
concepts.statement: Atoms moving through three spatially separated beams are adiabatically transferred into a controllable mixture of |3⟩ and |4⟩, whose different momentum kicks map the internal state onto position: a beamsplitter for atoms.

concepts.name: Adiabaticity condition with decay
concepts.statement: With decay γ₁₃ from the excited state, the first-order corrections to dark-state following scale as γ₁₃/Ω²τ, so adiabatic following requires γ₁₃/Ω²τ ≪ 1, quite different from the condition for coherent evolution.

concepts.name: Adiabatic expansion
concepts.statement: Expand the amplitudes in powers of a small parameter ∝ 1/τ: the zeroth order is the stationary solution with time derivatives neglected, and each correction is driven by the time derivative of the order before.

concepts.name: Error due to quantum jumps
concepts.statement: During the time τ the probability of a quantum jump is γ₁₃/Ω²τ, so the non-Hermitian evolution and the adiabatic approximation are valid in the same situations.

concepts.name: Fidelity of adiabatic passage with decay
concepts.statement: The probability of ending in −|2⟩ is ρ₂₂ = e^{−πγ₁₃/2|Ω|²τ}, which unlike the Landau-Zener result permits an expansion in the small parameter γ₁₃/Ω²τ.

concepts.name: Partially diagonalized basis
concepts.statement: The dark state |D⟩, the bright state |B⟩ and the excited state |E⟩ form a partially diagonalized basis in which only |B⟩ couples to |E⟩, with Rabi frequency √(|Ω₁|² + |Ω₂|²).

concepts.name: Nonadiabatic coupling of dark and bright states
concepts.statement: The finite pulse time couples |D⟩ to |B⟩ like a weak field with Rabi frequency Ω_NA = 1/τ.

concepts.name: Escape rate from the bright state
concepts.statement: Excitation to |E⟩ and its decay give |B⟩ a finite lifetime, with escape rate γ_B = Ω²/γ₁₃; the atom stays dark when 1/τ ≪ Ω²/γ₁₃, the same adiabaticity condition reached by reasoning physically.

concepts.name: Adiabatic following and EIT
concepts.statement: A probe pulse propagates through an EIT medium without loss only if it is longer than the inverse dark-resonance linewidth, τ ≫ γ₁₃/Ω², which is exactly the adiabatic following condition: the atoms follow the dark state in and back out as the pulse passes.

concepts.name: Dark state preparation by optical pumping
concepts.statement: A mixed state cannot be turned into the dark state by any Hamiltonian evolution, but optical pumping in the bright and dark basis prepares it by purely incoherent processes: atoms excited from |B⟩ decay into |D⟩ and remain.

concepts.name: Coherence as population in another basis
concepts.statement: A coherence in one basis is a population distribution in another basis; for linearly polarized light on a J = 1 to J′ = 1 transition, the dark superposition of m_⊥ = ±1 is exactly the state m_∥ = 0.

concepts.name: Classes of multi-photon processes
concepts.statement: Multi-photon processes fall roughly into three classes: incoherent interactions, where atomic coherences are not important; coherent interactions, where atomic coherences matter and two or more photons are required to generate them; and parametric interactions, where no energy is exchanged between light and atoms but the atoms mediate interactions between light beams.

concepts.name: Raman transition
concepts.statement: In a Raman transition two photons stimulate a dipole-forbidden transition via an excited state: by absorbing a photon on transition ν₁ and emitting a photon of frequency ν₂, population is coherently transferred between the two ground states.

concepts.name: Three-level configurations
concepts.statement: Two-photon transitions occur in three configurations of three levels: the Λ system, in which a single excited state mediates transitions between two lower states; the cascade system, climbing through an intermediate state; and the V system, two excited states sharing a ground state.

concepts.name: Λ system
concepts.statement: In the Λ system a single excited state |3⟩ mediates transitions between two lower states; the transitions to |3⟩ are dipole allowed and decay quickly, while |2⟩ → |1⟩ is dipole forbidden, so the metastable state |2⟩ can have a very long lifetime.

concepts.name: Single- and two-photon detunings
concepts.statement: The single-photon detunings Δ₁ and Δ₂ measure each field from its transition to |3⟩, and the two-photon detuning is their difference.

concepts.name: Λ-system Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: In the appropriate rotating frame, with the energy of |1⟩ set to zero, the Hamiltonian of the Λ system holds the detunings on its diagonal and the two Rabi frequencies off it.

concepts.name: Λ-system equations of motion
concepts.statement: Neglecting decay, a state c₁|1⟩ + c₂|2⟩ + c₃|3⟩ obeys the Schrodinger equation for the Λ Hamiltonian, giving equations of motion for the three amplitudes.

concepts.name: Effective two-photon Rabi frequency
concepts.statement: For large similar single-photon detunings Δ ≫ Ω₁, Ω₂, γ₃, δ the excited amplitude is eliminated and the two lower levels behave as a two-level system coupled by an effective Rabi frequency, each level Stark shifted by |Ω_i|²/Δ.

concepts.name: Λ-system density matrix equations
concepts.statement: To account for decay and dephasing the Λ system is treated with the density matrix: Liouvillians carry decay from |3⟩ to |1⟩ and |2⟩ and from |2⟩ to |1⟩, and each coherence ρ_ij decays at its own rate γ_ij.

concepts.name: Complex decay parameter
concepts.statement: The phase evolution and decay of each coherence are expressed together in a complex decay parameter, its real part the decay rate and its imaginary part the detuning.

concepts.name: Stochastic wavefunction treatment of the Λ system
concepts.statement: Decay from |3⟩ and |2⟩ enters a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, and its Schrodinger equation may be used so long as the probability of a quantum jump stays small: for a weak probe starting in |1⟩, or with slow decay from |2⟩ and little excited population.

concepts.name: Weak-probe steady state of the Λ system
concepts.statement: For a weak probe Ω₁ and a constant Ω₂ of arbitrary strength the system stays in |1⟩ to zeroth order in Ω₁, and Fourier transforming the equations of motion gives the two-photon and optical coherences.

concepts.name: Linear susceptibility on the probe transition
concepts.statement: When the probe is weak the response of the system is characterized by the linear susceptibility on the probe transition, proportional to ρ₃₁/Ω₁.

concepts.name: Two-photon resonance
concepts.statement: At large Δ the probe susceptibility shows, beside the broad single-photon resonance of width γ₁₃, a narrow two-photon resonance shifted to δ = |Ω₂|²/Δ; its width is set by the metastable decoherence γ₁₂ and an excited-state term strongly suppressed by the detuning.

concepts.name: Effective two-photon detuning
concepts.statement: The effective detuning of the two-photon resonance is the two-photon detuning less the light shift of |2⟩.

concepts.name: Two-photon resonance at the unitarity limit
concepts.statement: Exactly on two-photon resonance with no dephasing the susceptibility is that of a radiatively broadened system, approaching the unitarity limit, and the two-photon peak has the same amplitude as the single-photon resonance.

concepts.name: Dressed-state picture of the Raman resonance
concepts.statement: The strong field Ω₂ dresses |2⟩ and |3⟩; the single-photon resonance is the transition to |+⟩, nearly |3⟩ with nearly its radiative width, and the two-photon Raman resonance the transition to |−⟩, whose width is its dephasing rate.

concepts.name: Two-photon Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: For large detunings the three-level system behaves as an effective two-level system even for strong fields Ω₁ ∼ Ω₂; since the effective Rabi frequency scales as 1/Δ and the effective decoherence as 1/Δ², a detuning can always be found at which many Rabi oscillations occur before a quantum jump.

concepts.name: Raman coupling through many excited states
concepts.statement: With many excited states, far detuned, the eliminated system again behaves as a two-level system whose effective Rabi frequency sums the contributions of every excited state.

concepts.name: Doppler-free two-photon resonance
concepts.statement: A moving atom sees its detunings Doppler shifted; the two-photon detuning shifts by (k₁ − k₂)·v, almost nothing for co-propagating beams of nearly the same frequency, since the Raman process transfers momentum ℏ(k₁ − k₂).

concepts.name: Phase insensitivity of the Λ system
concepts.statement: The probe response depends only on |Ω₂|², not on the relative phase of the fields, because the two-photon coherence ρ₂₁ is free to follow the phase of the optical coherences; were |1⟩ → |2⟩ dipole allowed, the relative phase would matter.

concepts.name: Cascade two-photon resonances
concepts.statement: A far-detuned cascade system shows two-photon resonances too, but they are typically broader, since its final state usually decays by allowed emission, and their Doppler shifts cancel for counter-propagating beams, since both photons are absorbed.

concepts.name: Dark resonance
concepts.statement: With Ω₂ on resonance and the probe swept, the probe absorption vanishes exactly at two-photon resonance as γ₁₂ → 0, leaving a narrow dip in a broad absorption peak, while the coherence on the forbidden transition stays finite.

concepts.name: Bright state
concepts.statement: On resonance the excited state |3⟩ couples only to one superposition of the lower states, |B⟩.

concepts.name: Dark state
concepts.statement: The superposition of the lower states orthogonal to |B⟩ is decoupled from the excited state and so insensitive to its decay: an eigenstate of the effective Hamiltonian with zero energy, with no polarization on the |1⟩ to |3⟩ transition but a finite coherence on the forbidden one.

concepts.name: Dark resonance as quantum interference
concepts.statement: The vanishing absorption is a quantum interference: the excitations of |3⟩ by Ω₁ and Ω₂ interfere destructively, leaving the excited state unpopulated.

concepts.name: Dressed-state picture of the dark resonance
concepts.statement: A strong resonant Ω₂ makes dressed states |±⟩ ∝ |2⟩ ± |3⟩ split by 2Ω₂, and the probe sees two peaks; the picture does not explain why absorption vanishes exactly halfway between them.

concepts.name: Electromagnetically induced transparency
concepts.statement: Resonant probe light enters the medium, compresses by v_g/c and propagates slowly, dragging a spin coherence of the dark state, with almost no absorption: electromagnetically induced transparency, or slow light.

concepts.name: Group velocity in the transparency window
concepts.statement: Near the dark resonance the slope of the refractive index, controlled by the intensity of Ω₂, sets the group velocity, which falls toward zero as Ω₂ → 0 together with the width of the transparency window.

concepts.name: Adiabatic preparation of the dark state
concepts.statement: The dark state is |1⟩ when only Ω₂ shines and −|2⟩ when only Ω₁ does, so a system starting in |1⟩ under Ω₂ is already dark; by slowly decreasing Ω₂ while increasing Ω₁ the atom adiabatically follows the dark state into |2⟩, free of dissipation from the excited state, in a counter-intuitive pulse sequence.

concepts.name: Parametric processes
concepts.statement: In parametric processes no energy is exchanged between photons and atoms; the nonlinear response of the medium, a nonlinear black box, mediates interactions between optical fields, mixing them or generating harmonics and sum and difference frequencies.

concepts.name: Sum frequency generation
concepts.statement: Driving a two-photon transition with fields ν₁ and ν₂ makes an atomic coherence and a polarization oscillating at the sum frequency, which radiates at ν₁ + ν₂; it needs both single- and two-photon transitions allowed, which a broken inversion symmetry such as a Stark-mixed 2s–2p level of hydrogen provides.

concepts.name: Second-order nonlinear susceptibility
concepts.statement: The nonlinear susceptibility is the constant of proportionality between the sum-frequency polarization and the product of the two applied fields; whenever it is nonzero, two fields can generate the sum frequency.

concepts.name: Nonlinear susceptibility of the cascade system
concepts.statement: Far detuned from the intermediate states, the cascade system is a two-level system coupled by an effective two-photon Rabi frequency, with the Stark shifts in an effective two-photon detuning δ_eff, which gives its polarization and nonlinear susceptibility in terms of the dipole moments.

concepts.name: Undepleted pump approximation
concepts.statement: If the generated field is weak, the two applied fields act as pumps that are not greatly depleted, and their propagation is that of a linear medium.

concepts.name: Propagation equations for sum frequency generation
concepts.statement: For continuous-wave fields along z the total field is a sum of three slowly-varying amplitudes; the generated field grows from the nonlinear polarization and interacts linearly with the medium, and absorbing the linear terms leaves the pumps constant and the generated field driven with a phase mismatch.

concepts.name: Wavevector mismatch
concepts.statement: Δk is the difference of the total wavevectors of the three fields, the most important quantity determining the growth of the generated field.

concepts.name: Phase-matching condition
concepts.statement: When Δk = 0 the phase velocity of the generated field matches that of the polarization, which always adds constructively, and the field grows linearly with distance; otherwise the polarization slips out of phase after about π/Δk and the field interferes destructively. Equivalently, the process conserves momentum, k₃ = k₁ + k₂, as well as energy.

concepts.name: Coherence length
concepts.statement: For distances shorter than the coherence length, ΔkL ≪ 1, the system is phase-matched and the field grows linearly; beyond it momentum conservation fails and destructive interference sets in.

concepts.name: Competing processes
concepts.statement: The linear susceptibility, absorption and beam breakup compete with nonlinear generation and frequently overwhelm it, which in large part explains why nonlinearities in practical systems are often so small.

concepts.name: Sum-frequency output without phase matching
concepts.statement: Without phase matching the generated field peaks at z = π/Δk, set by the ratio of nonlinear to linear susceptibility; the two-photon detuning drops out, and the relative amplitude is of order Ω/Δ, very small.

concepts.name: Practical phase matching
concepts.statement: Phase matching is engineered through the linear dispersion: by mixing two gases, one for the nonlinearity and one for dispersion; by strong fields, as in EIT-like configurations that cancel the linear susceptibility; and in crystals by birefringence, temperature and angle tuning.

concepts.name: Saturation of the generated field
concepts.statement: Phase-matched growth cannot go on without bound: no energy is exchanged with the atoms, so the total intensity of the three fields is conserved, and the generated field saturates as it approaches the applied fields.

concepts.name: Difference frequency generation
concepts.statement: The same equations and phase-matching considerations apply to generating a lower difference frequency from a blue and a red field.

concepts.name: Density operator
concepts.statement: A system that occupies each of the quantum states |ψ_α⟩ with probability p_α is represented by a density operator, which can describe classical ensembles as well as quantum states.

concepts.name: Pure and mixed states
concepts.statement: If there exists a basis in which the density operator is |φ⟩⟨φ| the system is in a pure state; if not, it is in a mixed state; if the off-diagonal elements vanish, it is a statistical mixture of basis states.

concepts.name: Properties of the density operator
concepts.statement: Any density operator is Hermitian and has unit trace, and the inequality ρ̂² ≤ ρ̂ is an equality only for a pure state.

concepts.name: Expectation values from the density operator
concepts.statement: The expectation value of an observable is the trace of its product with the density operator.

concepts.name: Density matrix
concepts.statement: In a basis {|n⟩} the density operator is a matrix with elements ρ_{n,n'} = ⟨n|ρ̂|n'⟩.

concepts.name: Populations
concepts.statement: The diagonal elements ρ_nn of the density matrix are the probabilities of occupying the states |n⟩.

concepts.name: Coherences
concepts.statement: The off-diagonal elements ρ_nm are the expectation values of the coherence between levels |n⟩ and |m⟩, such as the atomic dipole operator.

concepts.name: Bound on the coherences
concepts.statement: A pure state has the maximal off-diagonal components allowed, the maximal coherence; a mixed state only satisfies the inequality.

concepts.name: Two-level atom in thermal equilibrium
concepts.statement: A two-level atom in thermal equilibrium is in a mixed state whose populations depend on the transition frequency relative to the temperature: well above k_BT/ℏ the atom is in its ground state.

concepts.name: Radiation field in thermal equilibrium
concepts.statement: A thermal mode of the radiation field is a statistical mixture of photon number states, so the expectation value of its annihilation operator vanishes.

concepts.name: Mean thermal photon number
concepts.statement: The average photon number of a thermal mode obeys the Bose-Einstein distribution.

concepts.name: Open system
concepts.statement: The universe is composed of the system and the environment, or reservoir, a large number of degrees of freedom over which we have no control; a system that interacts with its environment is an open system.

concepts.name: Reduced density operator
concepts.statement: The expectation value of a system operator can always be found from the reduced density operator, the trace of the universe density operator over the reservoir states; it need not describe a pure state.

concepts.name: Equation of motion of the density operator
concepts.statement: Under a Hamiltonian alone the density operator evolves by its commutator with the Hamiltonian.

concepts.name: System-environment entanglement
concepts.statement: Coupling evolves an initial product of system and environment states into a state that cannot be factored; the system and environment are then entangled.

concepts.name: Reduced state of a decaying atom
concepts.statement: An atom spontaneously emitting into the vacuum has a reduced density matrix whose off-diagonal elements decay at half the rate of the excited state population, as for any interaction that conserves energy.

concepts.name: System, reservoir and interaction Hamiltonians
concepts.statement: The total Hamiltonian is the sum of a system term, a reservoir term and an interaction term containing products of system operators with reservoir operators.

concepts.name: Evolution of the reduced density operator
concepts.statement: Tracing the equation of motion over the reservoir, the system Hamiltonian acts as it would alone, the reservoir Hamiltonian has no net effect, and the interaction requires special treatment.

concepts.name: Spin in a fluctuating magnetic field
concepts.statement: A spin whose splitting ħf(t) is a random field picks up a random phase on its off-diagonal element, which depends on the moments of f(t).

concepts.name: Stationary random process
concepts.statement: A random process characterized at each time by a probability distribution is stationary when its expectation value is constant; its variance describes the typical deviations from that average.

concepts.name: Correlation time
concepts.statement: The correlation time represents the timescale on which a random process changes: its variance ⟨δf(t)δf(t')⟩ is nearly constant for |t − t'| < τ_c.

concepts.name: Gaussian random process
concepts.statement: For a Gaussian probability distribution the mean and the variance specify all higher moments, which factorize pairwise; with zero mean all odd moments vanish.
