concepts.name: Reversible dephasing
concepts.statement: On times shorter than the correlation time each realization precesses at a random but fixed rate, so the ensemble dephases reversibly and a spin echo can undo it.

concepts.name: Markovian environment
concepts.statement: On times long compared to the correlation time the dephasing is irreversible; a reservoir with so short a memory is a Markovian environment, described by a Markov process with an infinitely short correlation time.

concepts.name: Interaction picture for an open system
concepts.statement: Transforming by the free evolution of system and reservoir leaves only the dynamics due to the interaction.

concepts.name: Bilinear system-reservoir coupling
concepts.statement: The interaction is a bilinear product of a system operator and a reservoir operator; in the interaction picture all its time dependence goes into the reservoir operator F̂_R(t).

concepts.name: Born-Markov approximation
concepts.statement: The reservoir is large, so it is not affected by the system and the universe stays factorizable, and broadband, so its correlation time is much shorter than the time on which the system evolves; averaging over a step τ_c ≪ ∆t ≪ τ_S then gives equations of motion for the system alone.

concepts.name: First-order reservoir term
concepts.statement: To first order the reservoir adds to the system Hamiltonian a term set by the mean of the reservoir operator, which vanishes for the atom-field interaction.

concepts.name: Reservoir correlation functions
concepts.statement: The second-order effect of the reservoir is written through two-time correlation functions of the reservoir operators.

concepts.name: Correlator of a thermal radiation field
concepts.statement: For a thermal radiation field the correlator depends only on the time difference and is sharply peaked, with width the reservoir correlation time; as the volume grows it becomes a delta function, the Wigner-Weisskopf approximation.

concepts.name: Master equation
concepts.statement: The master equation is the time-averaged equation of motion of the reduced density operator of a system coupled to a Markovian reservoir; it treats non-unitary behavior and preserves the trace.

concepts.name: Generalized master equation
concepts.statement: In the Schrodinger picture the master equation sums over incoherent system-reservoir interactions, each with its own rate γ_p, and adds the system Hamiltonian.

concepts.name: Cost of the master equation
concepts.statement: An n-level system needs n equations for its amplitudes, but O(n²) for its density matrix once the environment is included.

concepts.name: Factorization for a memoryless reservoir
concepts.statement: For a reservoir with no memory the correlations built up before an interval do not contribute within it, so the factorization assumption holds; corrections scale as τ_c².

concepts.name: Irreversibility as the system boundary
concepts.statement: A memoryless reservoir forgets all previous correlations, so information is lost and the dynamics are irreversible; any part of the environment that is time reversible is included in the system. The master equation may not suffice when interaction terms interfere or the reservoir interaction is reversible.

concepts.name: Master equation of a driven two-level atom
concepts.statement: A driven two-level atom coupled to a thermal field evolves under the coherent drive and the reservoir terms with Ŝ = σ₁₂.

concepts.name: Optical Bloch equations
concepts.statement: The matrix elements of the master equation give four differential equations for the density matrix, only two independent, with contributions from coherent driving, thermal photons and spontaneous emission.

concepts.name: Thermal and spontaneous transitions
concepts.statement: Thermal photons lead to incoherent transitions in both directions, whereas spontaneous emission only lets population leak from ρ₂₂ into ρ₁₁.

concepts.name: Decay rate of the coherences
concepts.statement: Incoherent processes only decrease the coherences, at half the sum of the population decay rates out of the two states, not into them.

concepts.name: Dephasing rate
concepts.statement: Processes that decrease the coherences without affecting the populations, such as a laser's finite linewidth or atom-atom interactions, enter the master equation phenomenologically as the decoherence or dephasing rate.

concepts.name: Weak-field response
concepts.statement: In a weak field the populations are frozen and the coherence at each frequency is a Lorentzian in the effective detuning, linear in the field like a classical dipole.

concepts.name: Steady-state coherence
concepts.statement: A constant field drives damped Rabi oscillations into a steady state, where the coherence follows the population difference.

concepts.name: Optical pumping rate
concepts.statement: The applied coherent field acts like an incoherent pumping rate R_opt.

concepts.name: Steady-state excited population
concepts.statement: With no thermal photons the steady excited state population is set by the ratio of the pumping rate to the decay rate.

concepts.name: Saturation
concepts.statement: A weak field leaves the atom in its ground state with an excited population proportional to the intensity; a strong field leaves an equal mixture of ground and excited states, and the response is saturated.

concepts.name: Rate equations
concepts.statement: When the coherences adiabatically follow the population difference, |Ω|² ≪ γ₂₁² + δ², the populations obey rate equations, as for an atom in incoherent radiation.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian of a moving atom
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian of an atom moving in laser light adds its centre-of-mass kinetic energy p̂²/2m and an external potential V(r̂) to the field and atom-field terms, and in the RWA the laser coupling Ω(r̂) = |Ω(r̂)|e^{iφ(r̂)} depends on the position operator.

concepts.name: Atomic recoil
concepts.statement: A plane wave of phase k·r couples |p⟩|1⟩ to |p + ℏk⟩|2⟩: absorbing a photon changes the atom's centre-of-mass momentum by ℏk as well as its internal state.

concepts.name: Recoil frequency
concepts.statement: The recoil frequency ω_R is the kinetic energy (ℏk)²/2m of an atom kicked by one photon, divided by ℏ.

concepts.name: Doppler and recoil shifts of resonance
concepts.statement: The transition |p⟩|1⟩ → |p + ℏk⟩|2⟩ is resonant at ω₁₂ shifted by the Doppler shift pk/m = vk and by the recoil shift ℏk²/2m.

concepts.name: Force operator
concepts.statement: In the Heisenberg picture the force on the atom is the commutator of its momentum with the Hamiltonian, which for the laser coupling is ℏ∇Ω|2⟩⟨1| + h.c.

concepts.name: Reactive and dissipative light forces
concepts.statement: Treating the atom as a classical ball feeling the average force, the light force splits into a dissipative part from the phase gradient and Im(ρ₂₁/Ω) and a reactive part from the intensity gradient and Re(ρ₂₁/Ω).

concepts.name: Validity of the semiclassical force
concepts.statement: The steady-state force on a classically moving atom holds for times long against 1/γ₁₂ and 1/δ and short against the recoil time, ω_R ≪ 1/t ≪ max(γ₁₂, δ).

concepts.name: Dipole force
concepts.statement: Far from resonance the force is reactive, the gradient of the AC Stark shift ℏ|Ω|²/δ; it is conservative and draws atoms to field maxima for δ < 0 and to minima for δ > 0.

concepts.name: Dipole trap
concepts.statement: A tightly focused red-detuned beam attracts atoms to its region of maximum intensity and confines them with little spontaneous emission.

concepts.name: Optical lattice
concepts.statement: A standing wave makes a periodic dipole potential with wells spaced by about λ/2, and orthogonal beams add dimensions: a model crystal of atoms and light.

concepts.name: Dissipative force
concepts.statement: In a plane wave the force is dissipative: a kick ℏk per absorbed photon, the spontaneous photon going into 4π, so the force is ℏk times the scattering rate, ℏkR_opt at low intensity, with the Doppler shift kv in the detuning.

concepts.name: Maximum dissipative force
concepts.statement: As the transition saturates the dissipative force reaches ℏkγ/2, since the atom spends at most half its time in the excited state.

concepts.name: Slowing an atomic beam
concepts.statement: Slowing a beam takes some 10⁴ kicks over milliseconds and about a metre, and the atom stays in resonance as its Doppler shift changes only if the laser is chirped or a varying magnetic field Zeeman-shifts it.

concepts.name: Doppler cooling
concepts.statement: Cooling needs a force that depends on velocity, slowing hot atoms more than cool ones; Doppler cooling takes it from the Doppler shift in the dissipative force.

concepts.name: Zero-velocity excitation rate
concepts.statement: R⁰_opt is the optical excitation rate of an atom at rest, 2γ₁₂|Ω|²/(γ₁₂² + δ²).

concepts.name: Doppler force at low velocity
concepts.statement: For k·v ≪ δ, γ₁₂ the dissipative force is a velocity-independent kick ℏkR⁰_opt plus a term in (k·v) whose sign does not depend on the sign of k.

concepts.name: Friction coefficient
concepts.statement: Two counterpropagating beams cancel the kicks and leave a viscous force ηmv_z, with friction coefficient η proportional to δ: red detuning cools and blue detuning heats.

concepts.name: Optical molasses
concepts.statement: Three orthogonal pairs of counterpropagating red-detuned beams give independent viscous forces along each axis and cool the atom in three dimensions.

concepts.name: Maximum friction coefficient
concepts.statement: The friction coefficient is largest near δ ∼ γ₁₂ and, at saturation on a radiatively broadened line, reaches ω_R/2, so atoms lose momentum at a rate of order the recoil frequency.

concepts.name: Capture range
concepts.statement: The capture range −v_c < v < v_c is the band of velocities effectively cooled, v_c being where the force is largest; v_c is about the dominant rate (γ₁₂, Ω or δ) divided by k.

concepts.name: Magneto-optical trap
concepts.statement: A magnetic field gradient Zeeman-shifts the levels with position, and cross-circularly polarized molasses beams on a J = 0 → J = 1 transition then push the atom back to the centre while cooling it.

concepts.name: Langevin equation
concepts.statement: Brownian motion of a heavy particle is a viscous drag −ηp plus a fluctuating Langevin force f(t) of zero mean whose correlation, in the rapid-collision limit, is 2Dδ(t − t′).

concepts.name: Diffusion coefficient
concepts.statement: The diffusion coefficient D measures the strength of the fluctuating force through ⟨f(t)f(t′)⟩ = 2Dg(t − t′), with g normalized to unit area.

concepts.name: Momentum spread under the Langevin force
concepts.statement: The mean momentum decays as e^{−ηt}, unaffected by the noise, while the mean square momentum relaxes to D/η, a kinetic energy D/2mη.

concepts.name: Einstein relation
concepts.statement: In thermal equilibrium the balance of damping and diffusion fixes the temperature, D = mηk_BT: dissipation at finite temperature always brings fluctuations.

concepts.name: Random walk
concepts.statement: Without friction the particle only receives kicks, its mean square momentum grows linearly in time and no equilibrium is reached.

concepts.name: Damped operators without noise
concepts.statement: Adding decay terms −γσ̂ to the Heisenberg equations of atomic operators makes their commutator decay exponentially, which is unphysical.

concepts.name: System operators coupled to a reservoir
concepts.statement: With H_SR = −R̂†Ŝ − Ŝ†R̂, any system operator Â evolves by its system Hamiltonian plus terms in the reservoir operator R̂, which for a two-level atom in the radiation field is Σ ℏg_j â_j acting on Ŝ = σ̂₁₂.

concepts.name: Reservoir operator in the Markov approximation
concepts.statement: Integrating the field modes, the reservoir operator is a free-field term plus a source term that, for a slowly varying system and a broad reservoir, becomes the decay (γ/2)Ŝ.

concepts.name: Quantum Langevin force
concepts.statement: The quantum Langevin force f̂(t) is the free evolution of the initial field modes: its mean vanishes in a thermal reservoir and its second moments are delta-correlated, n(ω)γ in normal order and (n(ω) + 1)γ in antinormal order.

concepts.name: Heisenberg-Langevin equation
concepts.statement: Substituting R̂ = iℏ((γ/2)Ŝ + f̂) into the system equation gives the Heisenberg-Langevin equation: every dissipation (γ/2)Ŝ comes with fluctuations f̂.

concepts.name: Equivalence with the master equation
concepts.statement: For a vacuum reservoir the expectation value of the Heisenberg-Langevin equation matches the master equation of an atom in vacuum term by term.

concepts.name: Generalized Einstein relation
concepts.statement: Writing the Heisenberg-Langevin equations as dÂ_μ/dt = d̂_μ + 𝓕̂_μ with ⟨𝓕̂_μ𝓕̂_ν⟩ = 2D_μνδ(t − t′), the diffusion coefficients follow from the deterministic evolution alone, for any system coupled to a Markovian reservoir.

concepts.name: Noise force on a laser-cooled atom
concepts.statement: For a two-level atom in a vacuum radiation bath the Heisenberg-Langevin equation of σ̂₁₂ carries the noise force 𝓕̂₁₂ = (σ̂₂₂ − σ̂₁₁)f̂, whose only nonvanishing moment is γδ(t − t′); it makes the light force fluctuate about its mean.

concepts.name: Fluctuating light force
concepts.statement: Eliminating σ̂₁₂ adiabatically, the fluctuating force is the noise force filtered by γ/2 − iδ, delta-correlated with strength (ℏk)²|Ω̃|²γ/((γ/2)² + δ²), Ω̃ = 2Ω counting both beams and absorption.

concepts.name: Momentum diffusion in laser cooling
concepts.statement: The momentum diffusion constant of Doppler cooling is 2(ℏk)²R⁰_opt: a random walk in momentum with steps ℏk at the rate of spontaneous emission.

concepts.name: Doppler cooling limit
concepts.statement: Through the Einstein relation the pumping rate drops out of the temperature, k_BT_D = ℏ(δ² + γ₁₂²)/2δ, smallest at δ ≈ γ₁₂ where k_BT_D = ℏγ₁₂: the Doppler limit set by the linewidth alone.

concepts.name: Laser attenuation in a dense sample
concepts.statement: An optically thick sample attenuates the cooling beams, so the forces acquire a spatial gradient: an extra dipole force and position-dependent cooling.

concepts.name: Spontaneous photon reabsorption
concepts.statement: A spontaneous photon reabsorbed by a nearby atom kicks it away from the emitter, an effective repulsion between atoms within about a wavelength.

concepts.name: Sub-Doppler cooling
concepts.statement: Alkali atoms were cooled ten times below the Doppler limit, in ways sensitive to the beams' polarizations and favoured by large detuning, pointing to the atoms' multilevel structure and AC Stark shifts.

concepts.name: Polarization gradient
concepts.statement: Two counterpropagating beams with crossed linear polarizations (lin⊥lin) make two cross-circularly polarized standing waves shifted by π/2, so the circular polarization changes with position.

forms.latex: \mathbf{E} = E_0e^{i\nu t}\left((\hat{x} + i\hat{y})\cos kz + i(\hat{x} - i\hat{y})\sin kz\right) + c.c.

concepts.name: Light-shift potentials of the ground sublevels
concepts.statement: On a J = 1/2 → J′ = 3/2 transition, unequal Clebsch-Gordan coefficients give the two ground sublevels different AC Stark shifts, and in the lin⊥lin field they become potentials ℏ|Ω|²/δ(1 − (2/3)sin²kz) and ℏ|Ω|²/δ(1 − (2/3)cos²kz) shifted by a quarter wavelength.

concepts.name: Sisyphus cooling
concepts.statement: The local polarization optically pumps the moving atom into the lower light-shifted sublevel, so it keeps climbing hills and loses the potential energy to the spontaneous photon.

concepts.name: Optical pumping between ground sublevels
concepts.statement: Rate equations for the ground populations relax the population difference Δρ at the rate 1/τ_P = (2/9)R_opt towards its local steady value cos 2kz.

concepts.name: Sisyphus cooling force
concepts.statement: The reactive force on the ground sublevels averages to zero if the populations follow their steady state; the lag τ_P of the moving atom's populations gives a velocity-dependent average force.

concepts.name: Sisyphus friction coefficient
concepts.statement: Solving the lagging populations exactly gives an average force with capture velocity v_c = 1/2kτ_P and, at low power, a friction coefficient η_S = 3(ℏk²/m)(δ/γ) independent of the intensity.

concepts.name: Doppler and Sisyphus cooling compared
concepts.statement: At low power and large detuning the Doppler friction vanishes as |Ω|²/δ³ while the Sisyphus friction grows with δ, but the Sisyphus capture velocity shrinks with the pumping rate |Ω|²γ/δ².

concepts.name: Non-adiabaticity in Sisyphus cooling
concepts.statement: Sisyphus cooling needs the populations to lag the atom's position: populations that adiabatically follow it gain downhill what they lose uphill.

concepts.name: Sisyphus cooling limit
concepts.statement: Diffusion from spontaneous kicks and from the fluctuating dipole force, set against η_S by the Einstein relation, gives k_BT_S ≈ ℏ|Ω|²/8δ: of the order of the depth of the light-shift potential.

concepts.name: Recoil limit
concepts.statement: An atom localized in one potential well has momentum uncertainty of order 2πℏ/λ, so the classical analysis stops at the recoil energy ℏω_R, far below the Doppler limit.

concepts.name: Sub-recoil cooling
concepts.statement: Cooling below ω_R needs a quantum treatment of the motion and uses two-photon transitions or dark resonances.

concepts.name: Fock states
concepts.statement: The eigenbasis of the field Hamiltonian is formed by the number states, or Fock states, each holding a definite number of photons in its mode.

concepts.name: Single-mode description
concepts.statement: Many properties of quantum fields can be understood from the evolution of a single mode, which is also quantitatively right for atoms in the field of a high finesse cavity.

concepts.name: Photon statistics
concepts.statement: The probability distribution for the number of photons in a mode, the diagonal of the field's density matrix in the Fock basis.

concepts.name: Single-mode thermal state
concepts.statement: A single mode in thermal equilibrium has a diagonal density matrix whose photon distribution falls exponentially with n, so zero photons is most likely, the mean is the Bose-Einstein n̄, and the mean field vanishes.

concepts.name: Multimode thermal light
concepts.statement: Summed over many modes, each most likely empty, a thermal field's total photon number is most likely finite and its distribution looks Poissonian; sunlight shows single-mode statistics only when filtered to a bandwidth Δω and detected in gates shorter than 1/Δω.

concepts.name: Coherent state
concepts.statement: The eigenstate |α⟩ of the photon annihilation operator, the quantum state of the classical coherent field of a laser, with a well-defined mean electric field.

concepts.name: Coherent amplitude
concepts.statement: The eigenvalue α of a coherent state: the mean field is proportional to it and the mean photon number is |α|².

concepts.name: Quadrature operators
concepts.statement: In analogy to position and momentum of an oscillator, x̂ and p̂ are the Hermitian combinations of â and â†; the field is x̂ cos ωt + p̂ sin ωt, so they are its in-phase and out-of-phase components.

concepts.name: Minimum uncertainty of a coherent state
concepts.statement: A coherent state has quadrature variances of 1/2 each, the most classical the uncertainty principle δxδp ≥ 1/2 allows; in phase space it is a disc of diameter √2 at a distance √2|α| from the origin.

concepts.name: Local oscillator
concepts.statement: A reference field cos ωt mixed with a signal, against which x̂ gives the in-phase and p̂ the out-of-phase component.

concepts.name: Shift operator
concepts.statement: The operator D̂(α) = exp(αâ† − α*â) displaces a state in the x̂, p̂ plane; acting on the vacuum it makes the coherent state, whose Fock expansion follows from the identity for exponentials of operators with c-number commutator.

concepts.name: Poisson statistics of a coherent state
concepts.statement: The photon number of a coherent state follows a Poisson distribution with variance equal to its mean |α|², so for large fields the intensity grows better defined.

concepts.name: Coherent state from a classical dipole
concepts.statement: A classical oscillating dipole driving the field evolves the vacuum by the shift operator, so the field it radiates is a coherent state with α = id₀E₀t/2ℏ.

concepts.name: Multimode coherent state
concepts.statement: A product of coherent states in every mode, whose mean field is the classical field with Fourier components E_k ∝ α_k.

concepts.name: Overcompleteness of coherent states
concepts.statement: The coherent states resolve the identity, (1/π)∫d²α|α⟩⟨α| = 1, but are not orthogonal, |⟨α|β⟩| = e^{−|α−β|²/2}, so they form an overcomplete set.

concepts.name: Quasi-probability distribution
concepts.statement: The density operator written as ∫P(α)|α⟩⟨α|d²α; P(α) always exists, gives normally ordered expectation values as a probability would, but can be negative.

concepts.name: Nonclassical states of light
concepts.statement: Negative values of P(α) are associated with non-classical properties of the field and mark a boundary between quantum and classical states.

concepts.name: Linear optical transformations
concepts.statement: Effects independent of the incident power, such as phase shifts and beamsplitters, under which a coherent state stays coherent; a phase shift takes â to âe^{iφ}.

concepts.name: Beamsplitter transformation
concepts.statement: A lossless beamsplitter with transmission t and reflection r mixes the two input annihilation operators linearly and unitarily (|r|² + |t|² = 1), so two coherent inputs leave as coherent states.

concepts.name: Beamsplitter as coupled oscillators
concepts.statement: The beamsplitter transformation is the unitary exp(iθâ₁â₂† + iθâ₂â₁†) of two coupled harmonic oscillators, θ set by t and r.

concepts.name: Cavity quantum electrodynamics
concepts.statement: A single atom confined in a high finesse cavity interacting with its single mode, an intrinsically anharmonic medium for the quantum field.

concepts.name: Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: The coherent coupling of a two-level atom to one resonant cavity mode in the rotating frame: absorbing a photon raises the atom, and the atom's relaxation emits one.

concepts.name: Jaynes-Cummings dynamics
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian couples each pair |2⟩|n⟩, |1⟩|n+1⟩ alone, which oscillates at g√(n+1); the general solution sums these pairs.

concepts.name: Vacuum Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: An excited atom in an empty cavity exchanges its excitation reversibly with one photon in a well-defined mode at the vacuum Rabi frequency g, unlike spontaneous emission into a continuum.

concepts.name: Strong coupling regime
concepts.statement: The regime in which the atom-cavity coupling g dominates dissipation: an excited atom gives its energy to the cavity mode faster than it emits into free space, g² > γκ.

concepts.name: Rabi oscillations in a coherent field
concepts.statement: Replacing √(n+1) by √n̄ for a coherent field leaves the field coherent and gives classical Rabi oscillations of the atom with period about 1/(g|α|).

concepts.name: Collapse of Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: The photon number spread δn makes each Fock component's phase g√(n+1)t differ; once gtδn/√n̄ reaches unity, about t ∼ 1/g, they dephase and the Rabi oscillations damp out.

concepts.name: Revival of Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: At longer times the phase corrections of the dominant Fock states reach multiples of π and the oscillations revive, imperfectly, at about 2π√n̄/g, a generic feature of isolated quantum nonlinear systems.

concepts.name: Field splitting in the Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: A coherent field interacting with the atom splits into two coherent components rotating in opposite directions in phase space, entangled with the atom, so the field no longer stays coherent.

concepts.name: Schrödinger cat state
concepts.statement: A superposition of two macroscopically distinguishable coherent states such as |iα⟩ ± |−iα⟩, with exponentially small classical coherence but higher order quantum coherence, easily destroyed by decoherence.

concepts.name: Beamsplitter model of loss
concepts.statement: Loss is a beamsplitter: the signal is attenuated by t while vacuum entering the other port adds fluctuations; a coherent state |α⟩ leaves as |tα⟩, but a Fock state does not stay a Fock state.

concepts.name: Cavity loss rate
concepts.statement: The rate κ at which the intracavity field energy leaks through a partially transmitting mirror, set by its transmission and the round-trip time.

concepts.name: Classical cavity field equation
concepts.statement: Counting one round trip, the intracavity field decays at κ/2 and is fed by the input field; its response is a Lorentzian of width κ, and a medium adds a polarization drive.

concepts.name: Input-output relation
concepts.statement: The output field of a cavity is the reflected input field plus the transmitted cavity field.

concepts.name: Quantum cavity mode equation
concepts.statement: Replacing the cavity field by â and adding the noise that goes with the decay gives a Heisenberg-Langevin equation: â decays at κ/2 and is driven by a noise operator.

concepts.name: Microscopic model of cavity loss
concepts.statement: Mirrors couple the cavity mode to continuum modes â_k with coefficients t_k; with Ŝ = â this is the spontaneous emission model, and the Wigner-Weisskopf approximation gives the decay rate κ = 2π|t_k|²D(ν) and the noise operator.

concepts.name: Cavity noise operator
concepts.statement: The cavity noise is the outside field leaking in through the mirror, the input field; in a thermal environment of n photons its correlators are (n+1)κδ(t−t′) and nκδ(t−t′).

concepts.name: Master equation of a damped cavity
concepts.statement: With Ŝ = â the general master equation describes cavity loss and its fluctuations, equivalent to the Heisenberg-Langevin description.

concepts.name: A coherent state in a lossy cavity
concepts.statement: A coherent cavity field decaying into vacuum stays coherent, |αe^{−κt/2}⟩: its mean decays while the quadrature variances stay 1/2.

concepts.name: Loss washes out nonclassical states
concepts.statement: Whatever the initial state, cavity loss drives the quadrature variances to 1/2, so squeezed and other nonclassical states lose their nonclassical coherence; generating them competes with dissipation.

concepts.name: Cavity mode driven by atoms
concepts.statement: Atoms in the cavity add a driving term to the mode's Langevin equation, the quantum analogue of the medium's polarization; for many atoms and strong fields this Heisenberg-Langevin approach is nearly classical, while for few photons and atoms the master equation or stochastic wavefunction serves better.

concepts.name: Open and closed cavities
concepts.statement: An open cavity confines the mode in one dimension (L ≫ λ), so the atom still decays to free space at nearly its free-space rate; a closed cavity confines the field in three (L ∼ λ) and can strongly suppress spontaneous emission.

concepts.name: Master equation of cavity QED
concepts.statement: The atom and cavity mode together form the system: Jaynes-Cummings evolution with the cavity detuned by δ, cavity loss at κ and atomic decay to free space at γ.

concepts.name: Dressed states of the Jaynes-Cummings ladder
concepts.statement: Each pair |1⟩|n⟩, |2⟩|n−1⟩ is a two-level system coupled by g√n and diagonalized on its own into dressed states; decay couples the manifolds and broadens them.

concepts.name: Vacuum Rabi splitting
concepts.statement: Probed in reflection, a resonant atom-cavity system shows its lowest dressed states as two peaks split by twice the coupling, 2g, the vacuum Rabi splitting.

concepts.name: Collective enhancement
concepts.statement: With N atoms at the cavity antinode the coupling grows to g√N and the vacuum Rabi splitting to 2g√N; classically, the atoms’ dispersion shifts the cavity resonance.

concepts.name: No-jump dynamics of cavity QED
concepts.statement: Starting from |2⟩|0⟩, only |1⟩|1⟩ is coupled coherently; with the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian of cavity loss and atomic decay the no-jump amplitudes evolve exactly, and for g ≫ γ, κ they show weakly damped vacuum Rabi oscillations.

concepts.name: Purcell effect
concepts.statement: When the cavity is overdamped, g < κ, eliminating the photon amplitude modifies the atom's decay rate and Lamb shift; in an open cavity at zero detuning the decay is enhanced by 4g²/κ.

concepts.name: Quality factor
concepts.statement: The cavity decay rate is the mode frequency over the quality factor Q.

concepts.name: Cavity finesse
concepts.statement: The finesse F is the mean number of times a photon circulates before leaking out; the photon lifetime 1/κ is F times the round-trip time.

concepts.name: Coupling to a cavity mode
concepts.statement: The atom-cavity coupling g grows with the dipole moment and falls as one over the square root of the mode volume.

concepts.name: Figure of merit for strong coupling
concepts.statement: The ratio g²/κγ is independent of the atom, ∼ (λ²/d²)F with d the mode diameter, largest for small cavities with high reflectivity; it is the chance that the atom meets the photon before the photon leaves.

concepts.name: Suppressed decay in a closed cavity
concepts.statement: In a closed cavity γ = 0 and the atom decays only through the cavity, at a rate strongly suppressed when the cavity is far detuned, by the quality factor when V ∼ λ³.

concepts.name: Microwave cavity QED with Rydberg atoms
concepts.statement: At microwave frequencies closed cavities are possible, γ ∝ ω³ is small and g ∝ √ω, and circular Rydberg states with large dipoles and second-long lifetimes give the highest ratio of coherent evolution to decoherence, provided thermal photons are removed.

concepts.name: Single photons on demand
concepts.statement: An excited emitter strongly coupled to a cavity emits one photon into the cavity mode’s direction, a bound-to-free problem whose wavepacket envelope decays at 2g²/κ; a three-level atom can shape it, and the process is coherent and reversible.

concepts.name: Hanbury-Brown-Twiss setup
concepts.statement: Splitting a signal on a beamsplitter onto two detectors measures joint probabilities: a single photon never registers on both at once.

concepts.name: Second-order correlation function
concepts.statement: The normalized intensity correlation g⁽²⁾ of the field at two points and times, which factorizes for coherent states and is sensitive to a higher order coherence than a laser's classical coherence.

concepts.name: Bunching and antibunching
concepts.statement: g⁽²⁾(0) is 1 for a coherent state, 2 for a thermal state (bunching) and 0 for a single photon (antibunching).

concepts.name: Noise of a linear amplifier
concepts.statement: A linear amplifier of gain σ > 1 adds noise from spontaneous emission that keeps the commutators fixed, so, as the no cloning theorem demands, a quantum state cannot be amplified without losing information.

concepts.name: Degenerate optical parametric oscillator
concepts.statement: Parametric down-conversion in a cavity at half the pump frequency, so both generated fields are the one cavity mode, driven by its own conjugate with gain β set by pump and χ⁽²⁾.

concepts.name: Phase-dependent amplification
concepts.statement: In the normal modes E₁ ± E₁* one is amplified and the other de-amplified at rate β̃, so the gain depends on the field's phase relative to the pump.

concepts.name: Quantum degenerate down-conversion
concepts.statement: For a strong classical pump and large detunings the Heisenberg-Langevin equations of a cascade atom in the cavity eliminate adiabatically to dâ/dt = −iβ*â†, the classical equation with E → â, from the effective Hamiltonian of photon-pair absorption and emission.

concepts.name: Non-degenerate down-conversion
concepts.statement: Two phase-matched modes amplified together obey dâ₂/dt = −iβ*â₁†, from an effective Hamiltonian that creates and destroys photons in pairs, one in each mode.

concepts.name: Photon pairs from down-conversion
concepts.statement: From the vacuum, non-degenerate down-conversion makes |vac⟩ + ξ|1,1⟩ + ξ²|2,2⟩ + …: correlated pairs from spontaneous emission for ξ < 1, stimulated emission and squeezing for ξ ≫ 1.

concepts.name: Correlated photon numbers
concepts.statement: Each down-converted mode alone is thermal, yet the photon-number difference of the two is exactly zero, far below the shot-noise limit n₁ + n₂ of a beam divided on a beamsplitter.

concepts.name: Heralded single photons
concepts.statement: Detecting a photon in one down-converted mode heralds precisely one in the other.

concepts.name: Post-selection
concepts.statement: Conditioning all later measurements on detecting both photons of a probabilistically generated pair, so that a polarization-entangled state is used only when it was made and not lost.

concepts.name: Squeezed state
concepts.statement: A degenerate down-converter amplifies one phase-weighted quadrature and attenuates the other, so a coherent state's variances change in opposite directions while their product stays 1/4; from the vacuum it holds only even photon numbers.

concepts.name: Squeezing in a damped cavity
concepts.statement: Cavity loss adds decay κ/2 and vacuum noise to each quadrature, so the squeezed variance approaches κ/2(κ + 2β̃) instead of zero.

concepts.name: Steady-state squeezing
concepts.statement: Below threshold, β̃ < κ/2, the intracavity variances reach steady values and squeezing is at most 50% at threshold, limited by vacuum leaking in; above it the undepleted-pump analysis fails.

concepts.name: Squeezing in the output field
concepts.statement: By the quantum input-output relation the reflected vacuum and the transmitted cavity field interfere, so at threshold and zero frequency the output quadrature is perfectly squeezed, over a Lorentzian of width ∼κ relative to the standard quantum limit.

concepts.name: Homodyne detection
concepts.statement: Mixing the signal with a strong local oscillator of phase φ on a 50/50 beamsplitter and subtracting the two photocurrents measures the signal's quadrature P_φ, amplified by the oscillator amplitude.

concepts.name: Squeezed light in interferometry
concepts.statement: With squeezing parameter r the quadrature noise falls to e^{−2r}/2, so the smallest measurable phase falls to e^{−r}/√n; in practice a stronger coherent field gives a similar gain more easily.

concepts.name: Spin squeezing
concepts.statement: For N polarized spin-½ atoms the collective spin's orthogonal projections fluctuate at the atom shot noise; interactions can squeeze one projection below it at the expense of the other.

concepts.name: Atom-photon correlations
concepts.statement: N-atom Raman scattering has the form of non-degenerate down-conversion between the photon mode and the collective spin, so detecting the photon heralds an entangled atomic excitation.

concepts.name: Confining ions
concepts.statement: Ions respond strongly to applied electric fields through the Coulomb force, which allows extremely tight traps, but one cannot create a static electric field minimum, so an ion cannot be confined by static electric fields alone; magnetic fields or RF electric fields provide the 3D confinement.

concepts.name: Penning trap
concepts.statement: The Penning trap confines the ion in two dimensions by its cyclotron motion in a magnetic field and in the third by charged endcaps; the crossed electric and magnetic fields add a larger-scale magnetron motion.

concepts.name: Quadrupole potential
concepts.statement: A quadrupole electric potential whose coefficients sum to zero by Laplace's equation, so that with α = −β, γ = 0 it confines in one direction and repels in the other.

concepts.name: Paul trap
concepts.statement: The Paul trap simulates an electric field minimum with a high-frequency quadrupole potential: averaged over many cycles of the oscillating saddle, the net effect is to confine the ion, in three dimensions with charged endcaps added.

concepts.name: Micromotion
concepts.statement: The ion follows the motion of the oscillating trap, 180 degrees out of phase with it, so it meets the repulsive potential near the centre and the confining one far from it.

concepts.name: Trapped-ion model
concepts.statement: For our purposes an ion trap can be approximated by a harmonic oscillator potential, the ion subject to laser excitation and spontaneous emission.

concepts.name: Cooling and qubit transitions
concepts.statement: A dipole allowed transition relaxes quickly and is used for laser cooling and for readout by fluorescence; a long-lived metastable state driven on a quadrupole transition, with lifetime around a second, is used for encoding information.

concepts.name: Internal and motional states
concepts.statement: The Hilbert space of the trapped ion is a two level system together with a harmonic oscillator ladder of Fock states describing its quantized motion.

concepts.name: Ion position and momentum operators
concepts.statement: The ion's position and momentum are written with the creation and annihilation operators of a quantum of vibrational energy in a trap of frequency ν.

concepts.name: Trap frequency
concepts.statement: The harmonic oscillator frequency ν of the trap, around 10 MHz for ions thanks to the strong Coulomb interaction.

concepts.name: Motional Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian of the ion's motion counts its vibrational quanta, each of energy ℏν.

concepts.name: Harmonic oscillator length
concepts.statement: The characteristic size of the ion's motional ground-state wave function, for tightly trapped ions significantly smaller than optical wavelengths.

concepts.name: Electronic Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: With spontaneous emission neglected, the ion's internal levels are a two-level system with ground state |g⟩ and excited state |e⟩ at ℏω_eg.

concepts.name: Negligible decay
concepts.statement: To neglect decay the rate γ must be small compared with the inverse of the manipulation time τ; this is reached with a metastable state driven on a quadrupole transition or with a far-detuned Raman transition, which reduces the effective linewidth by (Ω/∆)².

concepts.name: Ion-laser interaction
concepts.statement: The laser field acts at the ion's position, so x becomes the operator x̂ in the interaction Hamiltonian, for a running wave or a standing wave.

concepts.name: Momentum kick
concepts.statement: Absorbing a photon gives the ion a momentum kick ℏk, which can excite higher vibrational states, so laser excitation manipulates the centre of mass motion.

concepts.name: Lamb-Dicke parameter
concepts.statement: The ratio of the ion's spatial extent to the laser wavelength, a small parameter for tight traps; it is also the square root of the recoil frequency over the trap frequency.

concepts.name: Lamb-Dicke regime
concepts.statement: The limit in which the ion is so tightly bound that a photon's recoil energy cannot excite a higher vibrational state, so the photon momentum is absorbed by the trap rather than the ion; the real expansion parameter is η√n.

concepts.name: Trapped-ion Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: In the rotating frame the trapped ion's total Hamiltonian is the motion, the detuned internal level and the laser coupling, with η in the exponent for a running wave or in the sine for a standing wave.

concepts.name: Bare ion spectrum
concepts.statement: The bare states |g⟩|n⟩ and |e⟩|n⟩ are the ground and excited electronic levels, well separated since ω_eg ≫ ν, each subdivided into motional states spaced by ν.

concepts.name: Carrier and sideband couplings
concepts.statement: To lowest order in η a running wave couples |g⟩|n⟩ only to |e⟩|n⟩ with strength Ω and to |e⟩|n±1⟩ with strengths ηΩ√(n+1) and ηΩ√n; the three transitions are addressed individually by tuning the laser, and the sideband Rabi frequency grows with the phonon number.

concepts.name: Bare-resonance transition
concepts.statement: With the laser on the bare atomic resonance and weak enough, Ω ≪ ν/η, the sidebands are suppressed and the internal and motional degrees of freedom decouple: the ion cycles between internal states without changing its motional state.

concepts.name: Red sideband as Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: On the red sideband the ion obeys a Jaynes-Cummings model, internal transitions accompanied by creation or annihilation of a phonon, with the vacuum Rabi coupling replaced by g → ηΩ.

concepts.name: Strong coupling with ions
concepts.statement: Since the coupling ηΩ grows with laser power, the strong coupling regime is significantly easier to attain with ion traps than in cavity QED, and the coupling can be switched on and off with the laser.

concepts.name: Anti-Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: On the blue sideband the ion obeys an anti-Jaynes Cummings Hamiltonian, internal excitation accompanied by emission of a phonon and vice versa.

concepts.name: Standing-wave couplings
concepts.statement: In a standing wave the phase φ of the wave relative to the trap minimum is a further control: at φ = 0 the vertical transitions are eliminated and only the sidebands remain.

concepts.name: Sideband cooling
concepts.statement: A laser on the red sideband of an allowed transition lowers the motional energy in every excitation cycle while emission goes into all three transitions, pumping the ion on average into the trap ground state, which is dark to the laser.

concepts.name: Resolved sidebands
concepts.statement: The cooling rate is set by the fluorescence rate γ, but cooling into the ground state requires γ ≪ ν so that off-resonant excitation of the direct and blue sideband transitions can be neglected; a second laser coupling the forbidden level to an allowed one tunes the effective emission rate.

concepts.name: Arbitrary motional state
concepts.statement: An arbitrary motional state of the ion, with coefficients c_n that could be a Fock, coherent, squeezed or Schrodinger cat state; engineering such states is crucial to quantum gates in an ion trap.

concepts.name: Pulse sequence
concepts.statement: Laser pulses on the bare and sideband transitions are a series of unitary transformations linking an initial state to a final one.

concepts.name: Swap onto the motion
concepts.statement: A π pulse on the red sideband swaps information from the internal state onto the motional state.

concepts.name: Preparing a motional state
concepts.statement: Working backwards from the target state, alternate red-sideband and bare-resonance pulses empty the highest rung of the oscillator into the next until all the population is in the ground state; the inverse sequence prepares the state.

concepts.name: Ion string
concepts.statement: Ions in one anisotropic trap repel each other into a string spaced by 5-10 μm, far enough for a focussed laser to resolve each, while the Coulomb interaction couples their motion into phonon modes of different frequencies and spatial forms.

concepts.name: Two ions in a trap
concepts.statement: Two ions feel the harmonic confinement and their Coulomb repulsion, which to lowest order in their displacements from equilibrium adds a spring between them.

concepts.name: Centre-of-mass and stretch modes
concepts.statement: The two ions vibrate in a centre-of-mass mode at frequency ν and a stretch mode at √3ν, the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of their displacements.

concepts.name: Two-ion Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: Each ion's laser couples its internal state to both phonon modes, with its own Lamb-Dicke parameter per mode, and the two modes can be separately addressed by choosing the laser detuning.

concepts.name: Qubit
concepts.statement: A two-level quantum system storing information, its internal states read as bit values |g⟩ = |0⟩ and |e⟩ = |1⟩ and the information encoded in the state α|0⟩ + β|1⟩.

concepts.name: Universal computation
concepts.statement: If each qubit can be addressed and rotated arbitrarily, universal computation needs only one non-trivial gate coupling any two-qubit pair.

concepts.name: π phase gate
concepts.statement: The two-qubit gate that flips the sign of one qubit's excited state only if the other qubit is also excited.

concepts.name: Phase gate requirements
concepts.statement: The trapped-ion phase gate needs the vibrational modes cooled to the ground state and an auxiliary level degenerate with the excited state, coupled to the ground state by an orthogonal laser polarization.

concepts.name: Ion-trap phase gate
concepts.statement: A phase gate between ions m and n writes qubit m onto the collective motion with a red-sideband π pulse, applies a 2π pulse to the auxiliary level of ion n conditional on the motion, and writes the motion back onto qubit m, leaving the state unchanged unless both qubits were excited, when it changes sign.

concepts.name: Laser cooling
concepts.statement: Light can cool atoms: its forces not only slow them but narrow their velocity distribution, until a limit set by each scheme's heating.

concepts.name: de Broglie wavelength
concepts.statement: At low temperature the atoms are best described as matter wavepackets, whose size is set by the de Broglie wavelength.

concepts.name: Condensation criterion
concepts.statement: The transition between primarily classical and primarily quantum mechanical behaviour occurs when the atomic wavepackets overlap, at a density and temperature where the phase space density reaches ζ(3/2) ≈ 2.612.

concepts.name: Atomic density
concepts.statement: The density n of a gas counts its atoms per unit volume.

concepts.name: Critical temperature
concepts.statement: Below the critical temperature T_c set by the gas's density, a macroscopic number of Bose atoms occupy the lowest energy state, even at finite temperature.

concepts.name: Bose condensation
concepts.statement: Bose condensation, a macroscopic occupation of the lowest energy state, occurs only if the atom cloud is both dense and cold, so that its phase space density is large.

concepts.name: Indistinguishability and statistical weight
concepts.statement: The weight of an arrangement is the number of ways it can be formed; for ten particles in two states the {5, 5} arrangement outweighs {10, 0} by 252 when they are distinguishable, while for indistinguishable particles the two have equal weight.

concepts.name: Bose-Einstein distribution
concepts.statement: In the grand canonical ensemble N Bose particles with total energy E distribute themselves among the energy levels ϵ_i in the most random way, the Bose-Einstein distribution.

concepts.name: Chemical potential
concepts.statement: The chemical potential μ fixes the number of particles in the grand canonical ensemble; a gas and a surface in equilibrium have equal chemical potentials.

concepts.name: Keeping the ground state out of the integral
concepts.statement: When the sums are converted into integrals over the density of states g(ϵ), the atoms in the ground state ϵ₀ must be kept as a separate term.

concepts.name: Condensate fraction of an ideal gas
concepts.statement: For non-interacting, unconfined bosons the ground state holds N(1 − (T/T_c)^{3/2}) atoms below T_c; in a three-dimensional harmonic trap the power is 3.

concepts.name: Superfluid helium as a depleted condensate
concepts.statement: Superfluid helium is a strongly correlated fluid in which only about 10% of the atoms are in the ground state: a Bose condensate with a strong quantum depletion imposed by the interactions.

concepts.name: Condensation as a metastable state
concepts.statement: In thermodynamic equilibrium every material becomes solid or liquid before it is cold and dense enough to Bose condense, so a gaseous condensate must be a metastable state that lasts long enough to measure.

concepts.name: Spin-polarized hydrogen
concepts.statement: Spin-polarized hydrogen cannot recombine into H₂ and stays polarized for days; it was cryogenically cooled on superfluid helium walls and magnetically trapped, until spin-flip collisions on the walls stopped it at low temperature.

concepts.name: Stability window of the alkalis
concepts.statement: At very low densities and nano-Kelvin temperatures recombination needs a three-particle collision, whose rate is small beside the two-body elastic scattering rate, so the alkali gases can be evaporatively cooled to condensation.

concepts.name: Trapping and cooling
concepts.statement: Atoms must be cold to be trapped, and once trapped they can be cooled further because the trap breaks their thermal contact with the outside.

concepts.name: Atoms sticking to surfaces
concepts.statement: The potential above a surface supports many bound states into which an atom quickly relaxes, so above about 1 mK an atom that touches a solid sticks with probability essentially one.

concepts.name: Surface resonance time
concepts.statement: Equating the flux onto the surface with the rate of leaving gives the time an atom stays stuck, exponentially sensitive to its binding energy.

concepts.name: Trap depth
concepts.statement: The depth of a trap is expressed as the highest temperature of the atoms it can confine.

concepts.name: Buffer gas cooling
concepts.statement: A cold buffer gas cools any atom or molecule to its own temperature, near 1 K, before it reaches the chamber walls; the gas is then pumped away and the atoms held magnetically.

concepts.name: Magnetic trapping
concepts.statement: Magnetic traps confine atoms with nonzero angular momentum through the energy g_Fμ_Bm_FB_z; since Maxwell's equations forbid static field maxima, only weak-field-seeking states can be trapped.

concepts.name: Adiabatic following and Majorana flips
concepts.statement: An atom stays trapped if the field direction turns slowly beside the Larmor frequency; too fast a turn causes spin flips that eject it.

concepts.name: Quadrupole trap and its hole
concepts.statement: Anti-Helmholtz coils make a field linear in each direction with a zero at the centre, where adiabatic following fails, so the trap acts as if it had a hole; the time-orbiting potential (TOP) trap plugs it by moving the zero.

concepts.name: Ioffe-Pritchard trap
concepts.statement: A two-dimensional quadrupole combined with Helmholtz coils gives a nearly harmonic trap with a nonzero field minimum.

concepts.name: Evaporative cooling
concepts.statement: The atoms that boil off the top of the trap carry more than the average energy, so the remaining atoms re-thermalize to a lower temperature; lowering the barrier keeps the cooling rate up.

concepts.name: RF knife
concepts.statement: RF coupling to an untrapped hyperfine state, resonant where the trap's Zeeman shift matches it, cuts the hottest atoms from the edges of the trap; sweeping the frequency moves the knife toward the centre, a Landau-Zener crossing that limits the trap depth.

concepts.name: Competing loss processes
concepts.statement: Three-body recombination, inelastic (dipolar) collisions that flip the spin and background-gas collisions limit the lifetime of trapped atoms, so evaporation must be fast enough to finish but slow enough to let the atoms rethermalize.

concepts.name: Atoms in a linear trap
concepts.statement: In a spherical linear trap the thermal density falls as e^{−ηρ/ρ₀}, with η = μB₀/k_BT, so the trap holds 6V₀n₀/η³ atoms: η³ is a compression factor over the geometric volume.

concepts.name: Two-body inelastic loss
concepts.statement: Two-body losses go as the square of the density, so the dipolar loss from the trap carries a factor 1/8 beside the atom number.

concepts.name: Evaporation rate
concepts.statement: Atoms evaporate as fast as elastic collisions, with cross-section σ_el, refill the pool of hot atoms.

concepts.name: Good and bad collisions
concepts.statement: Atoms lost to dipolar relaxation heat the sample, so evaporation succeeds only if the evaporative loss beats the inelastic loss, which needs a favourable ratio of elastic to inelastic rates, g_in ≪ g_el, as in the alkalis.

concepts.name: Absorption imaging
concepts.statement: Imaging the shadow of the cloud in a resonant beam measures its transmission e^{−d/2}, set by the optical depth.

concepts.name: Time-of-flight imaging
concepts.statement: Released from the trap, the cloud expands and maps its initial momentum distribution onto position, which is then imaged; its shape tells the parabolic condensate from the gaussian thermal cloud.

concepts.name: Phase-contrast imaging
concepts.statement: Off resonance, the cloud imprints a phase φ = −δd/2 on the beam that interference with a reference reads out, exciting so few atoms that one condensate can be imaged many times.

concepts.name: Dilute quantum gas
concepts.statement: In a dilute gas the interatomic spacing is large beside the range r₀ of the van der Waals tail, and below the degeneracy temperature n^{−1/3}r₀ ≪ 1 implies kr₀ ≪ 1, the small parameter of the scattering theory.

concepts.name: van der Waals potential
concepts.statement: Between well-separated neutral ground-state atoms the dipole-dipole interaction in second order gives an attractive potential falling as 1/r⁶.

concepts.name: Collision as scattering off a fixed potential
concepts.statement: When the centre of mass decouples, a collision of two atoms is a single body of reduced mass μ = m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂) scattering off the fixed potential U(r).

concepts.name: Scattering amplitude
concepts.statement: Far from the scatterer the wavefunction is the incident plane wave plus an outgoing spherical wave weighted by the scattering amplitude f_k(θ).

concepts.name: Scattering cross-section
concepts.statement: The partial cross-section is the scattering rate into a solid angle over the incident intensity, |f_k(θ)|² for elastic collisions, and its integral over all angles is the total cross-section, an area.

concepts.name: Born approximation
concepts.statement: Expanding in the potential, the scattering amplitude is the Fourier transform of the potential; at low energy only the first term survives, so the scattered wave is isotropic.

concepts.name: Partial wave expansion
concepts.statement: For a spherical potential the wavefunction expands in Legendre polynomials into uncoupled radial equations, solved separately inside and outside r₀ and matched where r₀ < r < 1/k.

concepts.name: Scattering phase shift
concepts.statement: Each partial wave leaves the potential with a phase shift δ_l fixed by the matched coefficients, which vanishes as k → 0, and the scattering amplitude is a sum over them.

concepts.name: s-wave dominance
concepts.statement: In the ultracold limit kr₀ ≪ 1 the partial amplitude f_l ≈ cr₀(r₀k)^{2l}, so all but the s-wave amplitude f₀ may be neglected unless a resonance intervenes.

concepts.name: s-wave scattering length
concepts.statement: The s-wave radial wavefunction outside the potential goes as 1 − a/r; the scattering length a is the intercept of its asymptote and alone characterizes s-wave scattering.

concepts.name: Signs of the scattering length
concepts.statement: A hard sphere has a = r₀, a finite repulsive potential 0 < a < r₀, and a shallow attractive well with no bound state a negative a; each new bound state changes its sign.

concepts.name: s-wave pseudopotential
concepts.statement: In the ultracold limit every potential with scattering length a acts like a delta-function pseudopotential, whose first-order shift is the mean-field energy and gives the chemical potential.

concepts.name: Scattering of identical particles
concepts.statement: For identical particles the two scattering angles add with ε = ±1, so identical bosons see their s-wave cross-section doubled and identical fermions do not interact in the s-wave channel.

concepts.name: Matter wave through a cloud of atoms
concepts.statement: A matter wave crossing a dilute slab of scatterers picks up a phase as light does in a medium, corresponding to the mean-field energy 4πℏ²an/m.

concepts.name: Cold, dilute and strongly interacting
concepts.statement: Where the scattering length far exceeds r₀, ka ∼ 1 while kr₀ ≪ 1: a gas that is cold and dilute yet strongly interacting, purely through the s-wave channel.

concepts.name: Weakly bound state
concepts.statement: For large positive a the resonance is tied to a weakly bound state of the van der Waals tail with energy −ℏ²/2μa², into which molecules can be formed.

concepts.name: Feshbach resonance
concepts.statement: When a bound state of a closed channel nears the threshold of the open channel, a small coupling between them makes the scattering length diverge; tuning a magnetic field moves the resonance and so controls the interactions.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian of a dilute Bose gas
concepts.statement: A weakly interacting dilute gas is described by single-particle terms and two-body interactions, the latter replaced by the s-wave pseudopotential of strength U₀ = 4πℏ²a/m.

concepts.name: Second quantization of matter
concepts.statement: Creation and annihilation operators add or remove an atom from single-atom states; their commutation (bosons) or anticommutation (fermions) builds the symmetry of the many-body wavefunction in.

concepts.name: Matter field operator
concepts.statement: The Fourier transform of the momentum-mode operators is the field operator ψ̂(r), which annihilates a particle at position r.

concepts.name: Second-quantized Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: With the s-wave pseudopotential the gas's Hamiltonian is a single integral over the field operator.

concepts.name: Non-interacting condensate at T = 0
concepts.statement: Without interactions every atom piles into the single-particle ground state, the Gaussian of the harmonic trap with oscillator lengths a_j² = ℏ/mω_j.

concepts.name: Gross-Pitaevskii equation
concepts.statement: When the field operator is close to a classical coherent field and its fluctuations are small, the condensate obeys a Schrödinger equation with a nonlinear term, its wavefunction ψ normalized to the atom number.

concepts.name: Symmetry-breaking description
concepts.statement: Replacing ψ̂ by the c-number ψ assumes the atom field is a coherent state with an arbitrary phase and an uncertain atom number, valid for large atom numbers.

concepts.name: Ground state of a condensate
concepts.statement: Atom number is conserved, so the ground state is a stationary solution of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation evolving at the chemical potential; the ratio of mean-field to trap energy, ∼ Na/a_t, sets its character.

concepts.name: Trap length and frequency
concepts.statement: A harmonic trap of frequency ω_t has a characteristic size a_t, the oscillator length of its ground state.

concepts.name: Thomas-Fermi approximation
concepts.statement: For strong repulsive interactions the kinetic energy is neglected and the density is (μ − V)/U₀ where V < μ; in a harmonic trap the chemical potential and the size grow with Na/a_t.

concepts.name: Healing length
concepts.statement: Near a wall the condensate falls off smoothly over the healing length ξ, where the kinetic energy of the variation matches the interaction energy; in a dilute gas it spans many atoms.

concepts.name: Condensate density
concepts.statement: |ψ(r)|² is the condensate's spatial density, n₀ in a uniform condensate.

concepts.name: Bogoliubov approximation
concepts.statement: Linearizing the Heisenberg equation in small fluctuations δψ̂ about the mean field and expanding them in bosonic normal modes gives the Bogoliubov equations for the condensate's excitations.

forms.latex: \delta\hat{\psi} = e^{-i\mu t/\hbar}\sum_j\left(u_j\hat{\alpha}_j e^{-i\omega_j t} - v_j^*\hat{\alpha}_j^\dagger e^{i\omega_j t}\right)

concepts.name: Bogoliubov spectrum
concepts.statement: In a uniform condensate the excitations obey ℏω_q = √(ϵ_q² + 2n₀U₀ϵ_q): sound-like at small q and particle-like at large q, crossing over near the inverse healing length.

concepts.name: Free-particle energy
concepts.statement: ϵ_q = ℏ²q²/2m, the energy of a free particle of wavevector q.

concepts.name: Speed of sound in a condensate
concepts.statement: The sound-like part of the spectrum moves at s = √(n₀U₀/m).

concepts.name: Bragg probing of the spectrum
concepts.statement: Two lasers create a quasiparticle when their momentum and energy difference matches the spectrum, q = k₁ − k₂ and ω_q = ω₁ − ω₂, even at zero temperature.

concepts.name: Landau criterion for superfluidity
concepts.statement: An object can create an excitation only above a critical velocity, so objects moving slower than the speed of sound feel no drag: the repulsive condensate is a superfluid.

concepts.name: Stability of an attractive condensate
concepts.statement: With U₀ < 0 the long-wavelength frequencies are imaginary, but a trap of size a_t allows no wavevector below 1/a_t, so a condensate is stable up to N_max ∼ a_t/|a| atoms and collapses beyond.

concepts.name: Condensate and thermal cloud after expansion
concepts.statement: After expansion a condensate's size follows from the uncertainty principle, ∼ ℏτ/a_cm, while a thermal cloud is gaussian; fitting a bimodal distribution measures the condensed fraction.

concepts.name: First-order coherence of a condensate
concepts.statement: Two condensates with well-defined phases interfere like split laser light; thermal atoms are coherent only over about a de Broglie wavelength, while a condensate's long-range coherence spans the whole cloud.

concepts.name: Atom laser
concepts.statement: Outcoupling atoms by RF into an untrapped state gives the atomic equivalent of a laser beam; two RF frequencies outcouple from two places, and the visibility of their fringes measures the coherence between them.

concepts.name: Fringes of two expanding condensates
concepts.statement: Two condensates separated by ∆R_s expand and interfere with fringes spaced by ∆R ∼ ℏτ/∆R_s m.

concepts.name: Relative phase by measurement
concepts.statement: Two condensates of known atom numbers acquire a relative phase through spontaneous symmetry breaking in the measurement: detecting atoms without knowing their source projects the phase and leaves the numbers uncertain.

concepts.name: Double-well toy model
concepts.statement: N cold atoms in two wells joined by tunnelling at rate t, with ground state the symmetric |+⟩ and excited state |−⟩ higher by 2t.

concepts.name: Noninteracting ground state
concepts.statement: Without interactions all N atoms share |+⟩, a state with a well-defined phase between the wells that for large N is close to a coherent state: a classical Josephson device.

concepts.name: Strongly interacting ground state
concepts.statement: When U₀ ≫ t the atoms pile up evenly in the two wells in a highly non-classical Fock state, with no first-order interference and no Gross-Pitaevskii description.

concepts.name: Making non-classical matter
concepts.statement: Non-classical states of matter need interactions stronger than kinetic energy and low losses: tighter confinement, as in an optical lattice, lowers the tunnelling, and a Feshbach resonance raises the scattering length.

concepts.name: Optical lattice potential
concepts.statement: Counterpropagating red-detuned beams make standing waves of period λ/2 whose dipole force holds atoms at the intensity maxima; three of them make a simple cubic lattice, parameterized like the double well by tunnelling and on-site interaction.

concepts.name: Lattice site as an oscillator
concepts.statement: Near each minimum the lattice is harmonic with frequency ν_T; for depths V₀ ≫ E_R, the analogue of the Lamb-Dicke limit, atoms localize and wavefunctions on different sites barely overlap.

concepts.name: Recoil energy of the lattice
concepts.statement: E_R = ℏ²K_L²/2m, the energy scale against which a lattice's depth V₀ is measured.

concepts.name: Expansion in localized states
concepts.statement: The field operator is expanded over sites, ψ̂ = Σ b̂_i W(r − r_i), the Wannier functions approximated by each site's oscillator ground state; tunnelling hybridizes the levels into Bloch bands.

concepts.name: On-site interaction
concepts.statement: To leading order atoms interact only with those on the same site, with strength U₀ of about the interaction of two atoms in one oscillator ground state.

concepts.name: Hopping between sites
concepts.statement: Nearest-neighbour overlaps let atoms hop between sites at rate t, entering the Hamiltonian with a negative sign.

concepts.name: Bose-Hubbard model
concepts.statement: Site energies, hopping and on-site interaction together make the Hubbard model, realized by a Bose condensate in an optical lattice whose U and t are tuned by the scattering length and the lattice depth.

concepts.name: Superfluid in a weak lattice
concepts.statement: For t ≫ U₀ the hopping is diagonal in momentum, −2t Σ b̂_k†b̂_k cos ka, and every atom sits in k = 0: neighbouring sites are coherent, the phase is well defined and the number per site fluctuates.

concepts.name: Mott insulator
concepts.statement: For U₀ ≫ t at unit filling the ground state holds one atom per site, frozen in place, lowered by an exchange energy −2t²/U₀; the number per site is fixed, so the phase between sites is not.

concepts.name: Filling factor
concepts.statement: The filling factor ν is the number of atoms per lattice site; at commensurate, integer filling a Mott phase can form.

concepts.name: Quantum phase transition
concepts.statement: Changing t/U₀ moves the system between superfluid and Mott insulator even at T = 0, a phase transition driven by quantum rather than thermal fluctuations.

concepts.name: Mean-field estimate of the transition
concepts.statement: Comparing a product of coherent states with the Mott state predicts the transition near 4zt ∼ U₀; a variational state mixing 0, 1 and 2 atoms gives 5zt ∼ U₀, the mean-field value U₀/zt ≈ 5.8.

concepts.name: Excitation gap
concepts.statement: The superfluid has a Bogoliubov spectrum, while the Mott insulator's is gapped by ∆ϵ ∼ U₀ − t; the gap vanishes at the transition.

concepts.name: Wedding-cake structure
concepts.statement: In the harmonic trap of a real lattice the Mott phase forms shells of filling ν rising in steps toward the centre, with thin superfluid regions between them.

concepts.name: Observing the transition
concepts.statement: Released atoms of the superfluid interfere into the reciprocal lattice, while the Mott insulator, with no first-order coherence, shows no pattern; ramping U₀/t up and back recovers the superfluid.

concepts.name: Mean photon number
concepts.statement: The average number of photons in a mode, the mean of its photon distribution: the Bose-Einstein mean for a thermal state, |α|² for a coherent state.
